Senses.Explanation: A man of great resolve is an emphatic address for a man expected to act decisively. Ying’an Tanhua first recalls an interlocutor daring to stroke the tiger’s whiskers and Nanyuan’s hard-won achievement. He then adds another course: on the bare lump of flesh, cliffs stand ten thousand fathoms high; if someone from the assembly comes forward, strike that person across the back. He names the killing blade and the living sword and leaves their inspection to those with eyes. In the following hall address he contrasts wind splitting rock on Shaoshi Peak with a cold scene before the awakening hall, then concludes, ‘A man of great resolve cuts the matter in two with one stroke.’

Senses.PreferredTarget: Even when the great matter is clear, grieve as if your parents had died
SearchAliases: even when the great matter is clear, grieve as if your parents had died
Senses.Note: An old maxim says to grieve as if one’s parents had died both before and after the great matter becomes clear. Zishui says the second half demands even greater effort from those who understand. Yezhu asks why sorrow should remain after clarity. Chaozong voices the pair at a memorial sermon and turns the image toward those being remembered. Dounan questions whether repeating it is enough. Zhanran invokes it in a discussion of work after awakening. The mourning image presses the seriousness of what follows insight.

Senses.Explanation: The opening half of Muzhou's doubled mourning formula — with the great matter not yet clear, mourn as for parents — carried from his address to the assembly through centuries of re-deployment. Muzhou Daoming's address to the assembly fixed the doubled line — unclear, mourn as for parents; settled, mourn as for parents — raised verbatim in Baiyan Fu's collection of old-case commentaries; Zhongfeng Mingben absorbs both lines into his own ode and answers with mountains and rivers level as a palm, a straight official road, iron walls and silver mountains standing ahead for whoever asks about fortune; and Yezhu Fuhui proclaims the pair himself, concedes the unclear, then asks why the settled too should mourn, answering that at the time he only spoke of hair long and short — burn it and you know the ground was never level. Yunwai Xingze opens his small meeting with time flying and the seasons flowing, the great matter not yet clear, mourning as for parents, then asks who knows the light that never moves and the seasons that never flow; Yongjue Yuanxian warns that whether the great matter is yet unclear or one claims it settled, even overturning the world and toppling the buddhas and ancestors leaves the poison not yet dispelled; Guxue Zhenzhe names the unclear a knot — seizing empty space alive and knocking out blood — and the settled a loosing, the gnat swallowing the eastern sea; Chaozong Tongren, at the memorial service for a monk's parents, turns the doubled mourning into matched verses on the groundless dark craving and the wisdom that is idle furniture; and Yulin Tongxiu, staff raised, grants the old one's line and presses further — the settled still mourn, how much more the unclear — calling for the digging to be real digging and the waking real waking, food and sleep forgotten, to know one's own vast mind before the first thought.

Occurrences.Kwic: 網得脫，盡力行道，報佛之恩。次期，無限兵馬鋪山蓋地而至，軍中一官人姓張，近前問答，機言相投，接入營，送至仁懷，後入花壩山隱居。大眾！此非等閒，諸方被他劫奪綁縛，進營擔負，山僧感他恭敬，禮請進營供養。何也？莫不是山僧素行一點真實，不遭此凶神惡魔，而返來恭敬護法？彼花壩山係綦江、仁懷、桐梓三縣交界，實乃夜郎總府趙檀之地。初進山時，淒淒而上，捕鹿跡而踄，漸至山頂，倚樹相依。剛坐間，猛獸臨傍，入不思議色空無相定，諸境潛藏，邈無形跡。如是住三載，種種辛苦，未有剎那不在本念。所以古云：『大事未明，如喪考妣；大事已明，如喪考妣。』或時站立懸崖，或時經行露地，客來無迎送，饑寒失其時。行則直直無回互；坐則死死似癡愚。無理事不舉，有益話纔言，此是山僧數年前害的執著病。後轉綏陽，李總府及楊、趙留住萬佛山，予防人情難避，又恐攬繁嘈雜，即相謂曰：『山僧係是郊外蘆蓬之客，不熟人情，遂吾之志，方可住耶？』答曰：『隨師何志，無一不從。』遂住三載不下山。後又綦江程、熊、張、王、李五位總府接轉花壩建修，功果未就，仍遭饑亂，四方磨折，不得已下山，轉桐梓，蔡、李求度，同開佛現山。權住守時，雖道山水不分貴
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J39/J39nB471.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Daodeng of Konggu. Konggu Daocheng deploys the complete saying in a present recorded teaching turn.

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 網得脫，盡力行道，報佛之恩。次期，無限兵馬鋪山蓋地而至，軍中一官人姓張，近前問答，機言相投，接入營，送至仁懷，後入花壩山隱居。大眾！此非等閒，諸方被他劫奪綁縛，進營擔負，山僧感他恭敬，禮請進營供養。何也？莫不是山僧素行一點真實，不遭此凶神惡魔，而返來恭敬護法？彼花壩山係綦江、仁懷、桐梓三縣交界，實乃夜郎總府趙檀之地。初進山時，淒淒而上，捕鹿跡而踄，漸至山頂，倚樹相依。剛坐間，猛獸臨傍，入不思議色空無相定，諸境潛藏，邈無形跡。如是住三載，種種辛苦，未有剎那不在本念。所以古云：『大事未明，如喪考妣；大事已明，如喪考妣。』或時站立懸崖，或時經行露地，客來無迎送，饑寒失其時。行則直直無回互；坐則死死似癡愚。無理事不舉，有益話纔言，此是山僧數年前害的執著病。後轉綏陽，李總府及楊、趙留住萬佛山，予防人情難避，又恐攬繁嘈雜，即相謂曰：『山僧係是郊外蘆蓬之客，不熟人情，遂吾之志，方可住耶？』答曰：『隨師何志，無一不從。』遂住三載不下山。後又綦江程、熊、張、王、李五位總府接轉花壩建修，功果未就，仍遭饑亂，四方磨折，不得已下山，轉桐梓，蔡、李求度，同開佛現山。權住守時，雖道山水不分貴

ClaimAnchors.ClaimText: 大事未明，如喪考妣

Senses.Explanation: While the great matter remains unclear, grieve as if you had lost your parents. Press the urgency of resolving the great matter of life and death. Yunwai Xingze and Binya Jian use the complete saying in distinct recorded teaching turns. Yezhu Fuhui, Chaozong Tongren, and Konggu Daocheng give further current deployments. The inherited maxim also pairs this clause with a matching line after realization.

Entries.SourceTerm: 大事未明，如喪考妣；大事已明，如喪考妣

Senses.PreferredTarget: Before the great matter is clear, be as though mourning your parents; after it is clear, still be as though mourning your parents
AlternateTargets: Before understanding the great matter, as if bereaved of one’s parents; after understanding it, the same
SearchAliases: great matter before and after understanding mourning parents
before awakening after awakening as if bereaved
Senses.Note: The saying gives the same comparison for both sides of understanding: before the great matter is clear, and after it is clear, one is as urgent as someone mourning their parents. Its second half unsettles the idea that insight ends the work. Yezhu asks why the realized person would still feel this pressure; Zishui urges continued effort; Chaozong reads it as standing without a support; Chushi asks whether anything has been accomplished at all.

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 家住山住靜，為辦己躬，世緣盛衰，禪徒多寡，皆餘事耳。玅嚴雖半村半郭之地，既有蕭氏喬梓之賢，諒不以世故相責。在汝分上，正好借此一茅地，休歇身心，徹頭徹尾，參到大透脫、大安樂之地，方知山僧一向諄諄提策者，實無欺也。古人拈提大綱，汝非不知其概，第命根未斷，俱成法障，不能脫體現前，每為順逆境緣所奪。若不將前來理事兩岐底病痛一時坐斷，向千聖提掇不到處，撥轉乾坤，斬新日月，何有吾宗從上事哉？甲申春與諾諾導侍者甲申春與諾諾導侍者四方擾擾，賴佛祖之靈，山中猶獲晏然。本合親到天童掃塔，途路難行，故遣介石普演代之耳。《傳燈錄》自元至今未續，非奉旨無能編集。汝當為法門計，進京與諸護法共相維持。但得題請後，則諸方自各集而獻也。成與不成，雖有大數，然望汝竟成之，是所願也。至囑至囑。復定方龍居士復定方龍居士來教心切渴慕，莫繇從入，如窮子失父，煢煢無依，併冀慈悲開迷。雲指歇處者，不知秖此窮子失父，煢煢無依，乃真歇處，乃真入處，不必別求開指而渴慕也。古人云：「大事未明，如喪考妣；大事已明，如喪考妣。」豈非煢煢無依？正出息不涉眾緣，入息不居陰界，曾無間於未明已明，而惟此一事實乎？一念迴機，便同本得，人人無得處，原來一無所依。因不迴機自信，反慕禪道佛法已為依憑，故愈求愈遠耳。如今二六時中，但於世出世間一切法上，直下如斬釘截鐵，來無所粘，去無蹤蹟，唯自己一片靈明，自繇自在，不必問其歇與不歇，入與不入，自然瓜熟蒂落，噴地一發去也。但得此心嘗不昧，從教滄海變桑田。居士其力行之。復大也史監軍復大也史監軍來翰云：每至參不透處，幾以為大道玄遠，不可企及者。貧道謂：即此參不透處，便是當人實地處。但一迴機，當下即是，尚嗤太近，而何玄遠不及之足畏哉？此所謂道不遠人也。若捨此參不透處，而別求企及，則希冀之心不息，所謂人之為道而遠人矣。且問：如何是參不透處？試道看。又論：幸即自知振拔，而以汾陽三十年方纔成就之說為服膺。此長痼之藥，而非對症之藥；汾陽之說，為自恃天真知及，而仁不能守者，作頂門鍼也。若居士果知振拔，但當念古人云：「我立地待你搆去。」又云：「眨上眉毛，錯過了也。」又云：「現成公案，未入門來，早已三十棒了也。」恁麼見得，豈不以人治人？直下現成，方知從前見解，正是捨近圖遠；從前參求，正是怖頭狂走。果能與麼地，正好來高峰喫棒。未審居士耳否

ClaimAnchors.ClaimText: 大事未明，如喪考妣；大事已明，如喪考妣

Senses.Explanation: The same grief-like urgency appears on both sides of understanding. Yezhu challenges an easy reading of the old pair, while Konggu recalls it in describing his own unfinished work. Zishui calls for effort after recognition, Chaozong describes unsupported standing, and Chushi asks whether anything has been accomplished.

Entries.SourceTerm: 大人具大見，大智得大用

Senses.PreferredTarget: A great person has great vision; great wisdom finds great use
AlternateTargets: Great vision belongs to the capable person, and great wisdom works with great effect
SearchAliases: great wisdom works with great effect
Senses.Note: The two balanced clauses link a person of broad vision to wisdom that works in action. Masters use the inherited line for a patron's blessing, the work of a monastery, a funeral dedication, and a challenge to act without calculation. The point in these records is visible use, not a title automatically bestowed on every listener.

Senses.Explanation: ‘A great person has great vision; great wisdom finds great use’ joins insight to what it can do. These masters use the balanced line in ceremonies and instruction, then supply the particular action that makes it more than praise. Songyuan opens a verse for a patron with the line and praises timely public action. Linye cites it while setting aside calculation, then asks what word benefits the country and people. Yinyuan places it in a public blessing and says one word can meet many beings. Baichi uses it to describe a laywoman's ordinary capacity rather than a remote ideal. Qizhen gives it as he takes his seat at a robe ceremony. Lianfeng unfolds it into binding, releasing, and helping others; Zhangxue puts it in a funeral dedication for a patron's public work.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J37/J37nB389.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yuzhaoyunfen of Hongshan. Xiaotang Yunfen owns the retained answer: granted the great man's realm — truly different! — after his left foot, he answers by hanging down his right foot.

Senses.Explanation: The great man's realm of the Chan records: the sphere beyond reckoning — announced with a warning, catalogued with the first truth's names, granted to the two recluses, and answered with a hanging foot. Shengke Deyu announces the great man's realm to you — take it on just now, is that it? — and warns that gold dust in the eye becomes a film, so better no such good thing, Yuejiang Zhengyin catalogues it among the first truth's names — the king-of-summit concentration, the floating-banner king's ocean of realm-lands, the Manjusri-and-Samantabhadra great man's realm — then holds up one flower for the assembly and gets the golden kinsman's breaking smile, Muyun Tongmen grants it to Hanshan and Shide: the great man's realm is only for you to know and me to know — beggar's tricks, used to scaring ghosts with gods — and had Fenggan not gossiped, who to this day would know those two thieves, and Yingshan Zhiyin hands the layman the ox-and-horse verse of Dushun as the upward man's walking, the Manjusri-and-Samantabhadra great man's realm, asking whether his correspondent can accord with it — and if he can, moving by day like a dragon finding water, a tiger pacing the mountain, every step the play-sphere. Eryin Mi grades Yunmen as the elephant crossing the river, cutting through with every step traceless, against the head-seat as the fox on the ice, trembling forward and back and never done — then asks what the Manjusri-and-Samantabhadra great man's realm is: the sixteen-year beauty too lazy to comb her hair, letting her tangle hang — bone-fine to the end, wanton without powder — Zhufeng Huanmin rules the great man's realm interpenetrates, so the late-age temple should be planned, the mountain staff needing no ornament but the gate of the building-conversion wanting its arrangements, Cuiya Bi opens his installation by turning the formula both ways — the ancient buddhas' house style returns to the great man's realm, the great man's realm manifests the ancient buddhas' house style, the teaching following the teaching's own walking — and Xiaotang Yunfen, granted the great man's realm by his questioner's cry of truly different, answers by hanging down his right foot.

Senses.PreferredTarget: great rest and complete cessation
Senses.Explanation: Complete rest, with both resting and stopping reinforced. Yuanwu places it at the goal of direct instruction; Yulin applies it to Pang Yun; Miyun says someone truly there no longer measures time in ordinary terms. Tianyin, Baichi, and Huiyue independently use it for sustained practice, release from agitation, and free movement amid city life. Retained public meaning is supported by independent present uses in recorded discourse.
Senses.Note: Six distinct authored teachings are retained. No repeated case recension or lamp transport was added merely to meet the high-frequency depth floor.

Senses.Explanation: The great smelter's refined gold should show no change of color — Xuedou's seal cast at the close of his picking of Baizhang's three-day deafness, then fought over for six centuries: some rule the gold itself deserves a shout, some find one man in the age who can tell its color, and some stamp it on the faces of the beaten. Yuanwu Keqin, commenting on Xuedou's picking in his beat-the-rhythm record, carries the line to its close: you people — want to see the three-day deafness? The great smelter's refined gold should show no change of color. This one sentence has sunk how many men. Xuedou wants to let his breath out: he bares one device, one setting, unbreakable for a thousand, for ten thousand ages — do not mistake it, all of you. Xueyan Zuqin, retelling the same strike in his raising-old section, rules the age color-blind: from old till now the old masters under heaven cannot tell yellow from green, beans from wheat — only Xuedou came a little closer, saying the great smelter's refined gold should show no change of color. Then he tries the verses that followed: Fenyang's — tracing the outline, no maker. Zhenjing's — a man of great strength turns it over within speech and silence. Dahui's — speaking reason is one thing; to see Mazu and Baizhang, far, far off. Yuejiang Zhengyin raises the strike with Xuedou's whole picking inside it, then rules: the lion's cub-taming device — Mazu had it. Baizhang went three days deaf, and fine food does not fill a man already full. Xuedou said the great smelter's refined gold should show no change of color — good, and give it a shout. The Kebin family. Tianyin Yuanxiu raises the case — Xinghua tells the steward Kebin he will soon be a teacher of the assembly; Kebin will not enter the society; beaten, fined five strings of cash, a meal laid on, expelled — and voices Yunju Shun: the great smelter's refined gold should show no change of color; the pity is Xinghua's command runs too strict — had it not been Kebin, who could have borne it? Today's shallow crew — how long could they keep their faces from turning? Tianyin: plainly so, plainly so. Then Dahui's counter — Yunju bends the crooked into the straight; to make a blazing descendant of Linji, you must turn the face-skin — and Tianyin closes: the old man is not luring you into lawbreaking; do you all know where this lands? Meet a swordsman on the road, show your sword; to one who is no poet, never offer poems. And Wanru Tongwei, raising the same case with both comments inside it: Yunju and Jingshan only work the face-skin; the single move of Xinghua and Kebin — that they never grope their way to. And yet — luckily there was then a face to let them vine upon. Were there no face, where would the two old men be now? Xiaotang Yunfen, opening the furnace for the closed retreat at Hongshan: the worn-out old fire-seed has already shown its light — the great smelter's refined gold should show no change of color. Here the buddhas of the three times strip off their greasy caps; here the six ancestors shed their falcon-foul shirts; the old masters of all the ages, ring within ring, pass the fragrance on. You patch-robed ones, five to a pair — south of the river, north of the Huai, through Qi, Lu, Yan, Zhao, Wu, Yue, Min, Guang — what wind blew you today to Hongshan's gate?

Entries.SourceTerm: 大凡演唱宗乘，一句中須具三玄門

Senses.PreferredTarget: Whenever the lineage teaching is voiced, one sentence must contain the three mysterious gates
AlternateTargets: In proclaiming the Chan lineage, each sentence should carry the three mysteries
SearchAliases: one sentence three mysterious gates Linji
Linji three mysteries three essentials sentence
Senses.Note: Linji continues that each mysterious gate must carry three essentials, with authority and substance, illumination and use. Tianyin attacks a rigid parsing of the words; Tian'an asks how this relates to Linji's shout; Feiyin offers an expansive image instead of a diagram; Chaozong disputes later attempts to split the teaching; and Lianfeng asks what one would do before the lecturing seat. All selected passages quote Linji's exact words and then make distinct present comments.

Senses.Explanation: A great thousandfold world-system names the world-system quantified in the retained predicates. The exposition says that the merit grows continually into the future, that the person is personally predicted by the buddhas and protected and remembered by innumerable bodhisattvas, and quotes the treatise: one who hears this teaching without fear will certainly continue the Buddha lineage and receive a buddha's prediction. Its next comparative section supposes someone able to guide every being filling a three-thousandfold great-thousand world-system. The term therefore denotes the quantified cosmological domain in that comparison.

Senses.Explanation: The widest scale the records command: the whole world-system of the great chiliocosm, set up only to be carried, lit, covered, shrunk, or played in by a single staff, wheel, eye, or step. The oldest hinge is Yongjia's line that the great chiliocosm is a bubble on the sea and every sage a flash of lightning: Dahui Zonggao prices the right to speak it at sweeping every clean seat and ceasing to seek in Buddha, teaching, or community; Zhongfeng Mingben reads it as the test of standing in Yongjia's own time five hundred years on; Yinyuan Longqi asks what there is to first know once the bubble and the lightning have passed; Yuanwu Keqin gives the scale his own verse, one floating bubble where the eye stands high on the ten-thousand-fathom peak. The scale also works at full size: Tianyin Yuanxiu opens a Buddha's birthday address with the billion Sumerus of the chiliocosm reached without moving a step; Buhui Fatong answers the third of the three essentials with one wheel lighting the whole of it; Konggu Daocheng lifts his staff to cover it and hold the billion Sumerus up; Yun'e Xi lays it athwart a minnow's eye and stands the Sumerus inverted on a mosquito's lash at the closing of the retreat; Zhulang Chesheng takes it as the field of play with a hundred thousand years as one day; Zuliang Chaoqi rules that no net can hold it and calls for the one who will break through.

Senses.Explanation: ‘Vast worlds are bubbles on the sea; all sages flash by like lightning’ is a two-image line inherited from Yongjia's Song of Enlightenment. Later masters reuse it to unsettle the apparent size and lasting weight of both worlds and holy figures, often just before or after a present challenge. Gaofeng Yuanmiao sets the pair after a chain of numbers and barriers: if one sees through and jumps out, vast worlds and sages lose their hold; otherwise he urges another decisive turn. Yinyuan Longqi follows a sequence about seeing, hearing and knowing with the pair, then asks what his own impromptu address has exposed. Yunfu Daozhi laughs at the portrait someone has drawn of him and ends with the familiar pair. Huijue Yi strikes his staff after asking for a line that can show the universe in a hair's breadth, and answers with these images. Zhu'an Zhenyan adds his own comment to an older saying about worthies and follows it with the pair. Baiyu Jingsi opens his whisk into a circle, asks which collected virtue it shows, then lets the paired images answer.

Senses.PreferredTarget: Great is the primal power of Qian, from which all things begin
SearchAliases: great is the primal power of qian, from which all things begin
Senses.Note: The Changes praises the originating power of Qian, through which all things begin. Tian'an uses the line on New Year's Day to ask what the first character means. Baichi pairs it with Kun, the receptive counterpart, in a ceremonial sermon. Zixian raises a whisk while invoking it; Hansong uses it during a royal celebration and asks how to honor the occasion with one's whole body. The line supplies a beginning image that each teacher must still answer for.

Senses.Explanation: The Changes' praise of Qian as a source of beginnings becomes a ceremonial Chan opening. Tian'an asks the assembly about the beginning character, and Baichi joins Qian to Kun in the setting of a new court season. Zixian answers a festival question with the line while lifting a whisk; Hansong uses it at a royal festival and asks how the whole body honors the occasion.

Senses.Explanation: In the whole Great Tang realm there are no Chan masters. The charge is Huangbo Xiyun's own instruction: you are all wine-lees-gobbling fellows — wandering like this, where is there a today? Do you know that in the whole Great Tang realm there are no Chan masters? And when the monk demands what, then, of the honored ones everywhere herding followers, the answer that has never been improved on: not that there is no Chan — only that there are no masters. Yuejiang Zhengyin raises the whole exchange and caps it in a verse that opens on the tag itself: in the Great Tang realm, no Chan masters — wine-lees gobblers, fellows as many as Ganges sands; before the twelve peaks an old awl, brambles to the sky and no road to walk. Sanyi Mingyu, printing the exchange, rules against its author: Huangbo in one stroke gouged out the true-dharma-eye and sat himself on every critical ford — only to be crushed to powder by one squeeze of a wine-lees-gobbling fellow. Miyun Yuanwu's verdict is crueller: Huangbo is much dragon-head snake-tail — the moment that monk asked what of the honored ones everywhere, he should have been struck in the very sound of it; any hesitating, a blow across the spine: all that doting kindness — one may say, too much wine-lees. Baichi Xingyuan closes his raising with his own verse: the hand gripping the universe-sword, the breast holding sun-and-moon banners, deployed at the tip of the trigger where buddhas and patriarchs cannot peer in — wine-lees gobblers, do you know it or not? In the Great Tang realm, no Chan masters. Yunwai Xingze picks the case up under its own name: open-repairing the plank-road while secretly crossing at Chencang — that much he grants — but beware of calling a deer a horse; today this mountain monk spares no eyebrows and adds a footnote: great-smelter refined gold should show no change of color — Tuh! And Yulin Tongxu, the wild son of the story, stops the verger before the hammer-fall at his old master's hall and asks the charge turned on his own day: of old, in the Great Tang realm there were no Chan masters — in today's Great Ming realm, are there still any? The old master lifts his staff into a blow-pose — watch the staff! — and the two shout through the rounds until the boy walks out on his verse: not that the wild son has so much spirit — only that he has once passed the barrier above.

Senses.Explanation: The great earth with its mountains and rivers. Yuanwu Keqin says the buddhas of the three times attain the way within it and it emerges from that one place, Chushi Fanqi teaches that seeing form is seeing mind and that the earth-and-rivers are mind, and Liao'an Qingyu makes the array utterly precarious and the earth-and-rivers steeply dangerous at the summer release. Wuyi Yuanlai displays the whole mechanism in a grain of dust and the earth-and-rivers in a single blade of grass, Yongjue Yuanxian turns the sheet of snow into a lion's roar at the opening of the training season, Shanyi Ruchun opens the straight eye until no inch of soil remains, Yuan'an Liao reads the snowbound field where mountains are no longer mountains as the earth-and-rivers beaten into one, Huiyue Xu has it beg for its life under the true man's tread, Tianyin Yuanxiu caps Cao Shan's exchange by making it the very eye, and Ruibai Mingxue covers it over entirely where no one is seen at the Jinsu gate.

Senses.Explanation: A collapse formula naming the great earth sinking away at the breakthrough point, the standing lower half of the paired formula that shatters the sky. Gaofeng Yuanmiao's own self-account, recited by Yulin Tongxiu for the assembly, runs from the sixth day's loss of sleep and food to void shattered, earth sunk away, self and things both forgotten, like a mirror reflecting a mirror; Miyun Yuanwu's first-person record names the Copper-Coffin summit, where the sentient and insentient showed up evenly and not a flaw could be found, precisely the realm of the earth sunk away; and Tianyin Yuanxiu tells the trainee to hold one topic through walking, sitting, and lying until the nose is knocked loose, just like void shattered and earth sunk away, waking slowly to a first share of accord. Wuyi Yuanlai answers the questioning monk with law not law, mind not mind — knock over the lacquer bucket and the great earth sinks away; Baiyu Jingsi, taking up the staff at the season's binding, sinks the earth away and cuts off the thousand roads, the sea flows backward, Mount Sumeru stands on its head; Juelang Daosheng asks who, laying all heart down, would not have void shattered and earth sunk away, the body flung beyond the eon; Shiyu Mingfang tells the mourning household that a step further up the hundred-foot pole leaves no need to look back at the shattering and no room to doubt the sinking; and Jieweizhou Xingzhou, whisk raised, summons storm and rain till at one stroke the earth sinks away and the void shatters, asking how anyone could dodge it.

Occurrences.Kwic: 追薦，請上堂。僧問：「衣線下大事即不問，請法薦亡事如何？」師曰：「大地無寸土，鑊湯無冷處。」僧喝一喝，曰：「亡靈向者裏承當去也。」師曰：「看者漢今日死中得活。」乃揮拂子，曰：「昨夜霜天皎更清，今朝杲日照分明，靈光獨露常然顯，會取原來無死生。地獄哀兮豈可懼？天堂樂也不稱情，翛然撒手無為事，來往隨分任縱橫。為伊薦拔了也。」復豎拂子，曰：「看，看！陳氏眾等靈魂俱來山僧拂子頭上，同聲而說偈曰：『久在幽冥意未傾，辛酸受盡暗悲聲，今朝幸得無生法，生死出來一夢驚。』看看去也，且道向甚麼處去？樂邦留不住，遍界任騰騰。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J29/J29nB230.xml). Six-Session Record of Monk Shuijianhai of Tianwang. Shaweng Huihai gives the pair at a memorial requested for the dead. Asked how teaching can assist the deceased, he replies that there is no inch of earth and no cool place in the boiling cauldron. The monk shouts and says the deceased can take it up here; Shaweng says this fellow has found life amid death. His later poem denies a birth-and-death boundary and refuses to rest in fear of hell or attachment to heaven. He then stages the Chen family's spirits on the tip of his whisk, speaking a verse of release, and asks where they go. The pair's refusal of a safe foothold belongs to that enacted memorial teaching; the record does not present a literal cauldron in the room or independently verify the staged spirits' speech. The headword is rendered: Not an inch of earth anywhere; no cool spot in the boiling cauldron.

Occurrences.Kwic: 佛誕，上堂。僧問：「綠樹鶯聲似曲，雕梁燕語如簧。此景此時即不問，世尊降誕事如何？」師曰：「須彌山上擊金鐘。」進曰：「雲門道：『一棒打殺與狗子喫。』他具甚麼眼目？」師打，曰：「具者箇眼目。」進曰：「某甲即不然。」師曰：「你道看。」進曰：「家家門前赫日月，太平不用將軍威。」師曰：「你聽得須彌山上金鐘響麼？」僧罔對。師打，曰：「太平寰宇斬癡頑。」乃喝一喝，曰：「釋迦老子生也，便道：大地無寸土，鑊湯無冷處。天上天下，唯吾獨尊。」復喝一喝，曰：「雲門大師來也，便道：太平原是將軍定，那許將軍見太平？一棒打殺與狗子喫，貴圖天下太平。」又喝一喝，曰：「主山神來也，便道：世尊，你降生則已，何必矜誇？既大地無寸土，人人皆是佛。雲門，你雖謂正令提持，奈何棒頭短了，打他不著。今日因齋，不如大家慶贊。且道如何慶贊？」復喝一喝，曰：「誰人知此意？令我憶瞿曇。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J29/J29nB232.xml). Recorded Sayings of Monk Shuijianhai of Tianwang at Jinsu. The second occurrence is a birthday role-play authored and performed by Shaweng, not a historical quotation of the newborn Buddha. After a monk proposes peace without a general's force, Shaweng challenges and strikes him, then announces successive speakers with shouts. His imagined Shakyamuni says the exact earth-and-cauldron pair and 'I alone am honored.' His imagined Yunmen proposes killing him for the world's peace. The mountain deity then criticizes both: why boast, and why wield a staff that cannot reach him, when everyone is Buddha? The deity proposes that all join the celebration instead. The same pair now gives the dramatized Buddha an absolute declaration that the ensuing voices challenge. Its placement in this authored performance must remain distinct from Shaweng's own direct memorial reply. The headword is rendered: Not an inch of earth anywhere; no cool spot in the boiling cauldron.

Senses.Explanation: A fixed party-name that gathers the living beings of the whole great earth into one crowned, questioned, or saved party. Xueyan Zuqin crowns the true man who cuts the life-root of the buddhas and ancestors and stands as foe to the whole earth's beings while the hills stay green and the crows call, Zhongfeng Mingben has the Medicine Sage take the minister by the hand in the twelvefold vow sea and bring every being of the whole earth to right awakening inside one thought, Wuyi Yuanlai pours the great forge out in one mold till each being says a buddha has come into the world and each sees its own body made buddha, and Feiyin Tongrong hangs the sage's first words on the winter-eighth midnight, the beings of the whole earth already owning the sage's wisdom and virtue, then faults the sentence for splitting true and false apart. Miyun Yuanwu answers that the present buddha is the beings of the great earth and the future buddha not to be imagined, Weilin Daopei weighs the three-time buddhas as uneventful worldlings and the whole earth's beings as over-busy buddhas, eight ounces and half a pound on the whisk-tip scale, Baichi Xingyuan swallows the West River in one draught and asks where the fish and dragons hide, then kills the sand-count buddhas with one stroke and asks where the beings of the earth beg for their lives, and Yingning Zhijing would have stopped his ears at the newborn's claim to be the alone-honored one, leaving the whole earth's beings no edge to raise and no tongue to speak.

Senses.Explanation: Great ease is the repeatedly promised but sharply qualified freedom of one no longer driven about by circumstances; the records test it through ordinary eating and clothing, death and revival, and refusal to settle at a temporary stopping place. Guxue Zhenzhe says it is reached where tea, rice, warmth, and coolness are met as they come. Dahui Zonggao calls the person whose scheming route has died and who sits securely at home a person of great ease, while Yuansou Xingduan includes great ease among freedom, use, and release when no encountered thing can be obtained. The records also prevent an easy congratulatory reading. Xueyan Zuqin says even the opened gates are only temporary lodging and that a live road remains ahead toward great rest and great ease. Wuyi Yuanlai requires the wild-herdsman's condition beyond gathering ancestral treasures, and Chaozong Tongren asks how great ease could be obtained while an inherited explanation has hardened into a poisonous fixed thing.

Senses.Explanation: Everyone lend a hand to lift the broken sand basin. A communal call to take up the damaged vessel of the teaching and keep it functioning. The source-backed uses include Wanru Tongwei in J26nB182, Faxi Yin in J28nB221, Jie'an Jin in J29nB233, Zhufeng Fa in J38nB412, and Shanyi Ruchun in J39nB468. Each is a current use of the full line. The image keeps its paired structure across the records. The broken basin is a Chan image, not evidence of a historical repair project.

Senses.PreferredTarget: We are all right here
Senses.Note: “Everyone is right here” is a pointed answer, not merely a head count. Feiyin uses it for the final one of the five positions; Zhangxue says it when asked for the last word at the end of time. Chaozong says it when asked how saints and ordinary people gather. Yuan’an gives it for entering together, Muchen says it when an emperor asks where the three teachings meet, and Lüyan answers a question about arriving home with it. Each “here” belongs to that encounter.

Senses.PreferredTarget: Everyone fans themselves to catch a cooling breeze; why bind yourself when there is no rope?

Occurrences.Kwic: 解制，上堂。僧問：「薰風自南來，殿閣生微涼，明箇什麼邊事？」師云：「脫體了無依。」進云：「學人今日小出大遇也。」師云：「只得一半。」進云：「據虎頭、收虎尾不無，和尚卷舒覿露機鋒，如同電拂，又作麼生？」師云：「與汝三十棒。」進云：「出群須是英靈漢，敵勝還他天馬駒。」師云：「大眾識汝。」僧一喝，歸眾，師乃云：「日長饑有餘，夜短睡不足，熱汗急淋淋，蚊虫相齧鏃。大家搖扇取風涼，何用無繩而自縛？所以諸方此日結制安居，明發這裏解開布袋，雖則時節偶然，要且手腳便快。便快則不無，只如適纔藏主恁麼問，山僧恁麼荅，畢竟明箇什麼邊事？驢腮馬腳重重露，引得傍觀笑語高。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J28/J28nB202.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Baichi. At Baichi Xingyuan's release-from-retreat address, a monk asks what is revealed by the southern breeze cooling the halls. Baichi answers with complete freedom from dependence, yet says the monk has only half and threatens thirty blows as the exchange continues. His address then names long hungry days, short nights, sweat and biting mosquitoes: everyone fans for coolness, so why bind oneself without a rope? Although other places begin their retreat that day, his place opens its bag. He finally asks what the preceding questions and answers reveal. The headword joins an ordinary practical relief to criticism of self-imposed constraint; it does not settle the examination merely by praising comfort.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J38/J38nB430.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Qibaifu of Yuquan. In a spring instruction, Qibai Defu recites long days with hunger, short nights without enough sleep, pouring sweat and biting mosquitoes. Everyone fans themselves for a cool breeze, he says, so why tie oneself up without a rope? He immediately asks what his own words make clear and answers with donkey jowls and horse feet exposed again and again, while peach blossoms by the roof seem able to laugh at people. Unlike Baichi's longer retreat exchange, this brief turn records no monk's reply. Its practical invitation is checked by the teacher's question about the talk itself, rather than offered as an uncomplicated instruction to abandon discipline.

Senses.Explanation: “Great skill seems clumsy” (大巧若拙) sets accomplished skill beside the appearance of awkwardness. Yuanwu quotes the line while commenting that Baling’s answer was so sharply skillful that it returned to the appearance of clumsiness. Poshan sets it beside “great sound is rarefied” in an address. Zhaozhou Congshen receives the phrase as a presented condition and answers that the ridgepole timber is lost; Yikui places it beside “great wisdom seems foolish” in a winter-solstice address. Two verse collections also preserve the line as a capping phrase.

SearchAliases: a person of great thorough awakening
Senses.Explanation: The phrase is attested. It names an event or resulting qualification in biographies, appraisals, and questions. One record says that people of great thorough awakening have finished the matter of inquiry and afterward stayed by water and woods until pushed forward to address others (古人大徹大悟，參學事畢，且於水邊林下). A public exchange tests the qualification directly: Tianzhu says there is nobody of great thorough awakening in the hall; the record owner asks, "which one is not of great thorough awakening?" and the first counters, "which one is?" (那箇不是大徹大悟的；那箇是大徹大悟的). A Dahui record places it beside "the mind-ground opens and passes through" (大徹大悟，心地開通) and calls Zhaozhou's dog public case a key that opens that mind-ground. A later address jokes that its third phrase could make people greatly and thoroughly awaken, then refuses to utter it because nobody would remain to watch the Chan hall. These records attest the phrase as event, qualification, question, and comic hall claim; this entry adds no meaning beyond those recorded uses.

Entries.SourceTerm: 大徹底人本脫生死，因甚命根不斷

Senses.PreferredTarget: A person of complete realization has already left birth and death; why does the life-root remain unbroken?
AlternateTargets: If thorough awakening has freed one from birth and death, why is the root of life still not cut?
SearchAliases: Gaofeng six questions first life root birth death
Senses.Note: The original recorded-sayings source preserves this as Gaofeng Yuanmiao first room question. Yinyuan, Shipu, Dounan, and Pufu explicitly present their responses as answers or comments on Gaofeng six questions, each taking this first question separately. Gaofeng owns the quoted prompt, while the later masters are respondents. Life-root here is a Chan image for what continues to hold or animate a person; the line does not prescribe harm to a living body.

Occurrences.Kwic: 被毘尼纏縛，舉步踏殺眾生，瞎漢不妨疑著。人人有箇生緣，縱橫自在安然，日用光明歷歷，饑時喫飯倦眠。萬法歸一。五百東來五百西，一枝高出眾枝低，自從猿鶴歸來後，野鳥山雞不敢啼。一歸何處？萬法明明說向伊，霜風凜凜水生皮，團團紅日當空照，隔岸漁翁坐釣磯。雲林和尚小參，云：「一人辦道，忙殺伽藍。雲林八百禪和因甚日日絕糧？還是伽藍不靈？還是人不辦道？」幾百禪和住此山，阿誰不透祖師關？莫道伽藍不靈驗，日日絕糧頓頓餐。又舉：「大事未明，如喪考妣。大事已明，如喪考妣，因甚不見有一人哀戚者？」昨夜三更月到窗，曉來雪上又加霜，明明一片清平地，何事將軍急著慌。又舉：「青林和尚凡僧參見，先擔柴三轉，方乃入堂。還是教伊出坡？還是別有方便？」不是擔柴不是禪，法王法令驗愚賢，人天榜樣明今古，看破青林直甚錢。大隨庵側有龜，僧問：「一切眾生皮裹骨，者箇眾生骨裹皮。」師拈草鞋覆龜背上，僧無語。骨生肉外外生皮，六合乾坤陸地移，一隻草鞋輕覆卻，青天白日黑迷迷。高峰垂問六則大徹底人本脫生死，因甚命根不斷？大徹不大徹，燄裏寒冰結。凍殺天下人，通身冷似鐵。佛祖公案本是一箇道理，因甚明與不明？明與不明，羅什吞針。誌公啖鴿，少遇知音。大修行人當遵佛行，因甚不守毘尼？佛行毘尼本自遵，現成草料滿乾坤，雲門胡餅如天大，不搆師僧一口吞。杲日當空，無所不照，因甚被片雲遮卻？杲日當空無不照，白雲一片呈巧妙，乘風佈雨等尋常，本體太清仍皎皎。曹山三墮。走遍天涯海角頭，背駝星月望江遊，歸來踏斷曹溪路，超出人間第一流。喫油餈。喫些油餈飽，天明不覺曉，說向侍者知，庄主添煩惱。臨濟三頓。棒下叮嚀閃電機，梧桐風埽鳳離栖，大愚一拶翻身轉，當下還拳捋虎鬚。庭前柏樹子。祖師柏子應時機，惹得兒孫說是非，脫殼靈龜不費力，可憐鈍鳥逆風飛。萬緣放下。吹毛舉起命如絲，斬斷塵勞用幾時？大事未明須急急，萬緣放下莫遲遲。徹底掀翻是與非，三山四海總忘機，萬緣放下無尋處，石女溪邊把手歸。纔入靈山選佛場，萬緣放下即家鄉，默然忘卻來時路，不是愁人也斷腸。肇法師云：「天地與我同根，萬物與一體。」虛虛實實任君猜，根葉何曾有一枚。意氣不從天外得，金烏夜半照蒼苔。《維摩經》三十二，菩薩各說不二法門，文殊云：「我于一切法，無言無說，無示無識，離諸問答，是為菩薩入不二法門。」殊又問維摩，摩默然。殊

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 被毘尼纏縛，舉步踏殺眾生，瞎漢不妨疑著。人人有箇生緣，縱橫自在安然，日用光明歷歷，饑時喫飯倦眠。萬法歸一。五百東來五百西，一枝高出眾枝低，自從猿鶴歸來後，野鳥山雞不敢啼。一歸何處？萬法明明說向伊，霜風凜凜水生皮，團團紅日當空照，隔岸漁翁坐釣磯。雲林和尚小參，云：「一人辦道，忙殺伽藍。雲林八百禪和因甚日日絕糧？還是伽藍不靈？還是人不辦道？」幾百禪和住此山，阿誰不透祖師關？莫道伽藍不靈驗，日日絕糧頓頓餐。又舉：「大事未明，如喪考妣。大事已明，如喪考妣，因甚不見有一人哀戚者？」昨夜三更月到窗，曉來雪上又加霜，明明一片清平地，何事將軍急著慌。又舉：「青林和尚凡僧參見，先擔柴三轉，方乃入堂。還是教伊出坡？還是別有方便？」不是擔柴不是禪，法王法令驗愚賢，人天榜樣明今古，看破青林直甚錢。大隨庵側有龜，僧問：「一切眾生皮裹骨，者箇眾生骨裹皮。」師拈草鞋覆龜背上，僧無語。骨生肉外外生皮，六合乾坤陸地移，一隻草鞋輕覆卻，青天白日黑迷迷。高峰垂問六則大徹底人本脫生死，因甚命根不斷？大徹不大徹，燄裏寒冰結。凍殺天下人，通身冷似鐵。佛祖公案本是一箇道理，因甚明與不明？明與不明，羅什吞針。誌公啖鴿，少遇知音。大修行人當遵佛行，因甚不守毘尼？佛行毘尼本自遵，現成草料滿乾坤，雲門胡餅如天大，不搆師僧一口吞。杲日當空，無所不照，因甚被片雲遮卻？杲日當空無不照，白雲一片呈巧妙，乘風佈雨等尋常，本體太清仍皎皎。曹山三墮。走遍天涯海角頭，背駝星月望江遊，歸來踏斷曹溪路，超出人間第一流。喫油餈。喫些油餈飽，天明不覺曉，說向侍者知，庄主添煩惱。臨濟三頓。棒下叮嚀閃電機，梧桐風埽鳳離栖，大愚一拶翻身轉，當下還拳捋虎鬚。庭前柏樹子。祖師柏子應時機，惹得兒孫說是非，脫殼靈龜不費力，可憐鈍鳥逆風飛。萬緣放下。吹毛舉起命如絲，斬斷塵勞用幾時？大事未明須急急，萬緣放下莫遲遲。徹底掀翻是與非，三山四海總忘機，萬緣放下無尋處，石女溪邊把手歸。纔入靈山選佛場，萬緣放下即家鄉，默然忘卻來時路，不是愁人也斷腸。肇法師云：「天地與我同根，萬物與一體。」虛虛實實任君猜，根葉何曾有一枚。意氣不從天外得，金烏夜半照蒼苔。《維摩經》三十二，菩薩各說不二法門，文殊云：「我于一切法，無言無說，無示無識，離諸問答，是為菩薩入不二法門。」殊又問維摩，摩默然。殊

Occurrences.Kwic: 師回黃檗，舉前話，檗曰：「大愚老漢饒舌，待來痛與一頓。」師曰：「說甚待來，即今便打。」隨後一掌。檗曰：「者風顛漢來者裏捋虎鬚。」師便喝。檗曰：「侍者！引者風顛漢參堂去。」頌云：六十山藤敲不惺，一言撥動始知歸，還拳便掌風顛掣，坐斷乾坤獨震威。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J27/J27nB193.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yinyuan. Huangbo's threat comes when Linji returns after visiting Dayu and reports the encounter. Calling Dayu talkative, Huangbo says he will give him a beating when he comes. Linji refuses the delay: he will strike right now, and slaps Huangbo. Huangbo calls him a mad fellow pulling a tiger's whiskers, receives Linji's shout, and tells an attendant to take him into the hall. Yinyuan Longqi raises the case and verses that sixty staff blows did not awaken him but one saying stirred him to return; fist and palm disclose a fierce independent authority. Huangbo owns the quoted threat; Yinyuan supplies the present appraisal, not another threat to Dayu.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師回舉前話，檗曰：「大愚老漢饒舌，待來痛與一頓。」師曰：「說甚待來，即今便打。」遂掌。檗曰：「有風顛漢來者裡捋虎鬚。」師便喝。檗曰：「侍者！引這風顛漢參堂去。」三遭痛棒未開眸，一見高安當下休。有意氣時添意氣，當仁不讓轉風流。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J28/J28nB210.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Fushi Qiyuan. Fushi Qiyuan's record gives the same return encounter and its reversal of the promised beating into Linji's immediate palm. The response verse contrasts three unsuccessful beatings with the decisive meeting at Gaoan, then praises spirit answering spirit and taking responsibility without yielding. Its force falls on Linji's active return, rather than simply agreeing that Dayu deserves punishment. The exact words remain Huangbo's inside the old case; the verse is the current record's distinct handling.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J34/J34nB299.xml). Recorded Sayings of Monk Sanfeng Zang. Hanyue Fazang raises Huangbo questioning where Linji has been, hearing that he followed the instruction to visit Dayu, and responding with the headword. After Linji's slap and shout, Hanyue's verse pictures one step climbing a many-layered tower, the final provocation bringing swift flight, and the essential point breaking from a horn's tip. It ends by valuing what a true teacher hands on. The verse treats the rough encounter as a question of receiving and carrying teaching, without making Huangbo's literal promise a standing rule for how teachers should punish one another.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師回黃檗，舉前話，檗曰：「大愚老漢饒舌，待來痛與一頓。」師曰：「說甚待來？即今便打。」隨後一掌，檗曰：「者風顛漢來者裏捋虎鬚。」師便喝，檗曰：「侍者！引者風顛漢參堂去。」六十烏藤不肯休，三拳肋下豈輕酬，歸來依舊風顛樣，煞得滹沱正脈流。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J36/J36nB366.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Dafang. Dafang Xinghai raises the same threat and immediate blow, then writes of sixty dark staff strokes and three punches beneath the ribs that are not lightly repaid. Linji returns still in his mad style, but the verse concludes with the proper current of the Hutuo lineage flowing. The physical images belong to this old encounter and its appraisal; Dafang's cap interprets the apparent unruliness as part of transmission rather than a fresh instruction to strike someone in his own assembly.

Senses.Explanation: Huangbo's threat comes when Linji returns after visiting Dayu and reports the encounter. Calling Dayu talkative, Huangbo says he will give him a beating when he comes. Linji refuses the delay: he will strike right now, and slaps Huangbo. Huangbo calls him a mad fellow pulling a tiger's whiskers, receives Linji's shout, and tells an attendant to take him into the hall. Yinyuan Longqi raises the case and verses that sixty staff blows did not awaken him but one saying stirred him to return; fist and palm disclose a fierce independent authority. Huangbo owns the quoted threat; Yinyuan supplies the present appraisal, not another threat to Dayu. Fushi Qiyuan's record gives the same return encounter and its reversal of the promised beating into Linji's immediate palm. The response verse contrasts three unsuccessful beatings with the decisive meeting at Gaoan, then praises spirit answering spirit and taking responsibility without yielding. Its force falls on Linji's active return, rather than simply agreeing that Dayu deserves punishment. The exact words remain Huangbo's inside the old case; the verse is the current record's distinct handling. Hanyue Fazang raises Huangbo questioning where Linji has been, hearing that he followed the instruction to visit Dayu, and responding with the headword. After Linji's slap and shout, Hanyue's verse pictures one step climbing a many-layered tower, the final provocation bringing swift flight, and the essential point breaking from a horn's tip. It ends by valuing what a true teacher hands on. The verse treats the rough encounter as a question of receiving and carrying teaching, without making Huangbo's literal promise a standing rule for how teachers should punish one another. Dafang Xinghai raises the same threat and immediate blow, then writes of sixty dark staff strokes and three punches beneath the ribs that are not lightly repaid. Linji returns still in his mad style, but the verse concludes with the proper current of the Hutuo lineage flowing. The physical images belong to this old encounter and its appraisal; Dafang's cap interprets the apparent unruliness as part of transmission rather than a fresh instruction to strike someone in his own assembly. Senses.Explanation: True grace lies in good bone and bearing; even without rouge or powder, it has charm. Prefer intrinsic quality over cosmetic display. Fushi Tongxian and Buhui Fatong use the complete saying in distinct recorded teaching turns. Shipu Chaozhi, Hanxiu Ruqian give further current deployments. The phrase is a worldly poetic metaphor adapted to Chan judgment.

Senses.Explanation: The great expanse has nothing outside it. Mingjue Cong says it completely fills everything. Yuanwu Keqin pairs it with the great image having no form and compresses the world and empty space into objects held at hand. Hongzhi Zhengjue sets it beside a field without limit, while Junshan Xiansheng says it wraps the ten directions. The phrase marks an all-encompassing range; the four passages do not require a separate substance called the great expanse.

Senses.Explanation: Two records quote the proverb ‘before a person of great wisdom there are three feet of darkness’ when describing Chen Guan’s inability to explain two sayings despite his wide learning. Senses.Explanation: There is serious business ahead is a warning that failure to understand or premature claims of completion will have grave consequences. Chan masters place it directly after a failed test, an unresolved case, or an assertion that nothing remains to be done. Zishui warns those unable to understand two raised sayings; Juelang says that even producing escape lines for four cases leaves serious business; Shitian warns anyone unable to accept his summer instruction; and Yongjue rejects casual claims that eating and sleeping settle the matter.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X69/X69n1357.xml). Essentials of the Mind by Chan Master Foguо Keqin. In a direct letter, Yuanwu Keqin urges a capable reader to break through rather than be carried along by circumstances. He says that when the matter is put to use one can grasp great capacity, issue great function, move before a situation hardens, and turn things around. He follows with Yantou's saying about mastering rather than chasing objects. The headword names the responsive power Yuanwu says can be wielded; it is not a permanent faculty assigned to every person.

Senses.Explanation: Chan records tell a practitioner to “die the great death” by letting prior discriminations and supports fall away, but they repeatedly complete the image with coming alive, turning around, and responding freely. In the Blue Cliff Record, Yuanwu Keqin compares the condition to a greatly dead person who comes alive: long and short, good and bad are made one, yet fitting response is not lost. His recorded sayings similarly say that prior views and explanations must be put in order like a greatly dead person who can rise alive, after which contention falls away. Zhongfeng Mingben urges a practitioner to die the great death once and suddenly bite through the tasteless saying. Guting Shanmi says true and false then pass together without obstruction. Langting Ting denies that either cleverness or dullness can accomplish it and pairs the great death with turning back alive. Hanyue Fazang requires conditioned dust to fall away before one turns, emerges, and breathes freely; Tianran Hanshi likewise says one dies greatly and returns alive before elaborate inherited arrangements look like minor affairs.

Senses.Explanation: A person of great death is tested by the recurring question, 'When that person comes alive again, what then?' Zhaozhou asks it of Touzi, and other records preserve the same challenge with different respondents. Yuanwu uses coming alive after great death as a comparison. Hanyue Fazang criticizes people unwilling to relinquish themselves completely and become such a person; Guxue Zhenzhe contrasts the person of great death with the person of great life; and Chaozong Tongren calls the ordinary world, unchanged as heaven, earth, mountains, and waters, that person's field. The phrase is therefore not an ordinary corpse label: its force lies in the tested relation between complete death and renewed life.

Senses.Explanation: The floor of the great ocean of the Chan records: the impossible depth — the undrawn sword's still water, the paired formulas' horses and lamps, the snatched bird and the leaping wind god, and the warmth glowing under the sea while the north continent burns its fire. Shoushan Xingnian, asked how it is when the precious sword has not left its case, answers: on the floor of the great ocean, a still heart-mirror — and after it leaves the case, a sand-plover flicking its tail beyond the sky, Huiyue Xu, after the flick of the whisk and the dry-dung-chunk ask, adds one verse more: snatching the flying bird on the sea-floor, catching the swimming fish atop Sumeru, driving thunder and lightning on the midge's eyelash, one drop of water bursting open the azure vault's map, Pinjixiang Zhixiang sends the hunger-fast fundraiser off plainly — no need to buy clouds on the Wutai mountain, nor to seek water on the floor of the great ocean: you are all men of the way and virtue, gentlemen with an eye for finishing others' good, and Hengchuan Rugong addresses the patched-robe with the formula: horses run on Sumeru's mountain-top, the body hides on the floor of the great ocean — then the cremation fire for the stone-straight one, the ground bearing the mountain not knowing the mountain's loneliness, the stone holding the jade not knowing the jade's flawlessness. Liaotang Weiyi at the lantern festival answers the dream-sight ask with the same formula turned: horses run on Sumeru's summit, lamps are lit on the floor of the great ocean, Tian'an Sheng, granted the bright moon shown on the sea-floor and ten thousand miles of cloudless sky, asks where it was learned — and rules the whole-packed ask with last night's small assembly, today's hall, Pufu Zhuo grades the founders' display — the old barbarian gouging a wound in good flesh, Yunmen carrying firewood to the fire: always horses running on the sea-floor and boats rowing on Sumeru's summit, branch beyond branch, waves without wind — so by the mountain monk's view, twenty staff-blows each, demoted into the unborn kingdom, and Yushan Shangsi shows Shigong the archer frightening the wind god Sunyuo leaping into the sea-floor, the eight dragon kings rising to spread clouds and rain, sky and earth gone dark, rivers and seas surging — till archer and god alike land in the Mirror-Lake courtyard crying gained an ease, and he stamps them with the verse: third day, thirty-first, no need to pick the calendar; a night dream un-lucky, brush-write great luck.

Within a sequence of questions about Dayang Jingxuan's place, house style and teaching, a monk asks for Dayang's sentence that penetrates the body of reality. Dayang replies that red dust rises from the bottom of the great ocean and water flows across the summit of Mount Sumeru. Instead of an explanatory definition of that body, the reply gives paired images at the extremes of depth and height, making familiar relations of dust, water, bottom and summit difficult to settle into a single fixed picture. The record then moves to a separate question about Niutou and birds bringing flowers; it does not give a prose explanation of this couplet. Dayang is the original answerer. The complete reply has a job in this particular question that is not supplied by either constituent expression, ocean floor or mountain summit, on its own.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J39/J39nB454.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Pinjixiang. Pinjixiang Zhixiang raises the old monk's question and Dayang's full reply, then adds his own verse. The exact ocean-and-summit pair remains Dayang's quoted voice; this further sequence is Pinjixiang's present response. It places familiar uses of things alongside further impossible images while commenting on transmission without fabrication, rather than decoding the old reply into ordinary geography. The source gives no fixed one-to-one key for the images, so the explanation does not invent one. This is a distinct current treatment, while the other lamp biographies repeat the original encounter.

Senses.Explanation: The great sea does not retain a corpse: Linji Yixuan uses the sea's refusal to keep what is dead as a comparison for refusing what obstructs the person carrying it. Linji first warns the assembly not to misuse the mind, then gives this image and immediately says that people shoulder something, set out across the world, and raise their own view-obstructions against the mind. The saying is therefore not a description of the sea alone; in Linji's address it rebukes carrying dead weight into the search. The exact wording survives in several recensions of that same address, not in several independent encounters.

Senses.PreferredTarget: Great Nirvana Sutra
Senses.Explanation: The Great Nirvana Sutra is a scripture title, distinct from the phrase great nirvana without the scripture marker. Tianyin Yuanxiu raises a passage from the Great Nirvana Sutra about twelvefold causation and four levels of awakening. He asks how a Chan practitioner would respond beyond merely explaining its words, strikes his staff, and ends with an image of mountains and rivers meeting their source. The headword identifies the scripture Tianyin explicitly quotes; the scripture's old speaker is separate from Tianyin's present challenge. In a written reply to the teacher Qian San, Feiyin Tongrong recounts their earlier dispute over the Lotus Sutra's statement that worldly forms abide. Qian San had invoked the Great Nirvana Sutra to argue that arising and passing abide within what does not arise or pass. Feiyin uses the named scripture as the point of that earlier claim, then objects that it sets up two opposed levels and asks how this could express abiding. The headword is the scripture title in Feiyin's present account, while Qian San is the earlier interlocutor. In an instruction to the monk Hongchuan, Wuyi Yuanlai names the Great Nirvana Sutra and cites its account of a hidden treasury and the three inseparable qualities of release, the body of the thus-come one, and great wisdom. He then draws the lesson that the thus-come one's nirvana concerns the sentient mind and urges the student to realize it rather than settle for partial understanding. The headword identifies the scripture Wuyi quotes; the ancient scriptural voice and Wuyi's present explanation are distinct.
Senses.Note: The title includes the scripture marker; uses of the doctrinal phrase without that marker are separate.

Occurrences.Kwic: 悉皆罔措，故世尊云：「吾有正法眼藏，涅槃妙心，實相無相，微妙法門，不立文字，教外別傳，付囑摩訶迦葉，轉相傳受。」于是二十八祖達磨大師繼之乃云：「直指人心，見性成佛。」心既指矣，性既見矣，則從前所學所聞、所修所證，皆無復遺餘矣。然則座下以一刀欲殺其根株，是座下之所見，亦是古人之方便，非禪宗超方脫略極則之語，不知高明以為何如。又以老朽前詰《法華經》「是法住法位，世間相常住」之意重拈其說，殊不知法華一部七卷之文，以實相為宗，其他多贊揚表顯，唯此兩句經是的切顯實相之義。座下彼時驀指茶筵中云：「圓眼住圓眼位，糖餅住糖餅位。」老朽當時詰云：「圓眼一捏便碎，糖餅一喫便了，如何得常住？」座下彼時無對，少頃以《大涅槃經》為證大意，以生住異滅住於不生不滅為常住，彼時老朽詰云：「如是則生滅住於不生滅，則成兩法，遽成能所對待，如何得常住乎？」今座下以老朽似不肯其說者此也。今又以山水草木為世間相，妄情既除，山是真山，水是真水，草是真草，木是真木，天地未分，先有山水草木，乾坤既壞，山水草木不壞。據此不唯實相常住之旨未明，于世諦理義亦未盡意。既天地未分，又何從而有山水草木乎？乾坤既壞，又何從而有山水草木乎？況有妄情可除，又有真山真水，乃至真草真木；天地未分，又有山水草木；乾坤既壞，又有山水草木不壞，則岐然兩分，宛爾生滅與不滅生對待之法，如何是實相之道，得永遠常住乎？老朽如此引援辯詰，古賢所謂引而不發，只要當人于此悟明，

Occurrences.Kwic: 成。計果求菩提。是名顛倒見。見性元周遍，物體本虗無。斯見與見緣，悉妙淨明體。云何於是中，有是及非是，因緣和合非，皆成戲論想。識藏如來藏，真性了然故。毫端寶王剎，微塵轉法輪，是名報佛恩，豈待僧祇劫？欲究祖師禪，當提一句話，一口氣不來。畢竟甚處去？切上更加切，疑上更加疑。如坐鐵壁間，祇欲親迸出。一朝疑團破。捉賊驗真贓。雨打石人頭。剝剝論實事。世間出世間，如紅爐片雪，便好放癡憨。更不多饒舌。待了本因緣，再為仁者說。宗說等錫上。無異禪師廣錄卷第二十六無異禪師廣錄卷第二十七住博山法孫弘瀚彚編首座法孫弘裕同集宗說等錫下示弘傳禪人示弘傳禪人夫為學者，發大信心，成大力勢，於大乘圓頓法門，成辦大事。如覓諸味，先飲醍醐，復得餘食，知苦澀故。不然，於眾味中，而生足想，聞醍醐味，不生好樂之心也。大涅槃經云：我今當令一切眾生，悉皆安住祕密藏中，入於涅槃。何等名為祕密之藏？具三德故。如𠁼字，三點若並，則不成𠁼，縱亦不成。乃至解脫之法，亦非涅槃；如來之身，亦非涅槃；摩訶般若，亦非涅槃。我今安住如是三法，為諸眾生，名入涅槃。以此則知，如來涅槃，即眾生心。是佛說我者，即是覺義。以自心覺故，常樂淨義，悉備自心。故為眾生安住，非為佛安住也。如觀一微無體，真如性遍。觀者即般若，無體即解脫，性遍即法身。一塵中即具三德，即入涅槃。非縱非橫，圓融無礙。以此則知，一事一行，一一皆入法界，具無邊德。是無盡宗趣，性起法門，無礙圓通，實不思議。清凉大師云：凡聖交徹，即凡心而見佛心；理事雙脩，依本智而求佛智。或執理而迷事，或執事而迷理。而不知約圓明之智，成此事緣；又不知起行布之緣，求此理佛。當

Senses.Explanation: Great function or great use. In one public interview an unnamed monk asks Changqing Da'an what it is like when great function manifests without preserving rules. Changqing answers, “if you can use it, then use it” (汝用得但用); the recorded questioner bares his shoulder and is struck. Another unnamed monk asks Shanhui separately, “what is great capacity?” and “what is great function?” and receives a blow across the back for each. The corpus coordinates “great capacity and great function” (大機大用, 325 occurrences) and “the whole capacity and great function” (全機大用, 128 occurrences). Yuanwu Keqin uses the first pairing in instruction to Deshan Jing and the second while describing meeting life with life and death with death. Guishan Lingyou supplies an explicit contrast: “you people have obtained only the great body, not great function” (汝等諸人只得大體不得大用). Yangshan Huiji identifies Baizhang Huaihai with great capacity and Huangbo Xiyun with great function. Xuansha Shibei asks Xuefeng Yicun what it is like when great function manifests, and Xuefeng rolls three balls together. These formulas, questions, bodily replies, pairings, and contrasts show a function publicly displayed and appraised in encounters; they do not establish a separate metaphysical object behind the term.

Senses.Explanation: Great functioning appears is a formula that the records state, question, and qualify. Yuanwu Keqin says that when it appears, noise and quiet are one, like a boat going downstream without pole or oar. In the Blue Cliff Record he pairs the stock continuation ‘established rules are not retained’ (不存軌則) with using a blade of grass as a sixteen-foot golden body and the golden body as a blade of grass. A lamp account preserves Dazhu Huihai's direct equation: its appearing ‘is the unequalled body of the teaching’ (即是無等等法身). Dahui Zonggao also records a limit: students of sayings call Guizong's killing a snake and Nanquan's killing a cat instances of ‘great functioning appearing, with no established rules retained,’ but Dahui says that neither case is such a principle. The cited records do not make any one dramatic action its universal definition.

Senses.Explanation: Great doubt is an intensified mass of unresolved inquiry cultivated until its obstruction breaks open. Zhongfeng defines the category precisely: doubt itself has no large or small, but weighty doubt is called great doubt and light doubt small doubt. Wuyi says that when the faculty of trust is complete, a mind of great doubt arises; Poshan identifies what has not been clarified in scripture or penetrated in a case as the point from which this doubt develops. Baofu is asked about ‘a person of great doubt,’ and Minshu states the recurring proportion: great doubt brings great awakening, small doubt small awakening. The entry therefore names a recognized intensity of inquiry. A narrative such as 師大疑, where 大 simply modifies the verb ‘doubted greatly,’ is compositional and is not needed to establish the dictionary term.

Senses.Explanation: ‘Great gate of release’ names a way into freedom from binding. Masters use the gate image in sermons and written instruction, and sometimes stand at an actual temple entrance as they ask who can enter here and now. At a newly cast bell, Ying'an Tanhua links the gate to a bell's long-lasting reach and asks what the sound can accomplish. Yuanwu Keqin says one can enter after seeing and hearing without being caught by sights and sounds, then asks for a word on reaching home. Zhe'an Jingfan says the gate is right at one's feet, amid bustling streets and ordinary sights. Mi'an Xianjie invites all beings into a pure great gate during a dedication, then asks on what basis they may enter. Zhongfeng Mingben says the whole world can be such a gate once the mind is clear, but warns that merely repeating the sentence fails at the first difficult event. Yuansou Xingduan tells a lay inquirer that the gate has always been present in each person's share, though confusion makes it hard to use. Baiyu Jingsi stands at a monastery entrance, says he has opened the gate wide and asks how to enter. Hanxiu Ruqian also speaks at a temple gate: he points the way toward the light-filled hall, then asks who will walk with him.

Senses.Explanation: Not released in a general amnesty is Wuzu Fayan's answer to “What is the teaching?” The answer belongs to a three-part exchange: Wuzu answers “What is the buddha?” with “bare-chested and barefoot,” “What is the teaching?” with this phrase, and “What is the monk?” with “Third Brother Xie on a fishing boat.” Tianyin Yuanxiu later raises the full exchange alongside Dahui Zonggao's and Chushi Fanqi's comments. Sanfeng Zang's record transmits it under Wuzu's lineage heading, while Lingshuyuan's record has a fellow resident quote it before the record owner supplies three different answers. All four witnesses therefore preserve or discuss one answer rather than four independent uses.

Occurrences.Kwic: 趣分矣，即是規矩。天真而妙，一切皆然。特以眾生機有不同，便成頓漸，故宗趣分而規矩各殊矣。宗通趣極，真常流注。宗趣妙極，猶為理障，礙正知見，故名真常流注。玄沙曰：汝諸人須信有一分真常流注，亘古亘今，未有不是者，未有不非者。如此一句，成平等法。何以故？以言逐言，以理遣理，平常性相，說法度人。然猶明前不明後，未有出格之句，死在句中。外寂中搖，擊駒伏鼠。真常流注者，外觀似寂，中實搖搖，如繫駒不忘馳，伏鼠偷心在也。先聖悲之，為法檀度。隨其顛倒，以緇為素。顛倒想滅，肯心自許。只此肯心，便是金鎖玄路，故有十劫觀樹之事。要合古轍，請觀前古。佛道垂成，十劫觀樹。法華經云：大通智勝佛，十劫坐道塲，而諸佛法不現在前。過十劫已，諸佛之法乃現在前。曹山曰：未忘大果故。愚謂十劫表十成，過十劫表不滯十成。如虎之缺，如馬之馵。虎一名李耳，虎食畜不至耳，又每食人耳，則耳必一缺，此以例不敢犯諱也。馵者，馬後左脚間有白色也，此以例語忌十成也。以有下劣，寶几珍御。以有驚異，黧奴白牯。凡情聖見，是金鎖玄路，故先聖以法淘汰之。羿以巧力射中百步，箭鋒相值，巧力何預？射至百步，力也；射中百步，巧也。至箭鋒相值，則非巧力之所能及。木人方歌，石女起舞。非情識到，寧容思慮。此正明天真妙用，非智力所及，如箭鋒相值也。臣奉於君，子順於父。不順非孝，不奉非輔。此明當以偏輔

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 。山河大地，日月星辰，盡聖盡凡，都盧祇是一箇誰字，更無雜念。上下無路，進退無門。山盡水窮，情消見絕。豁然𪹼地一聲，方知非假他求。咄。示眾。閒花野草露真機，劒號巨闕。蛺蝶穿園拍板扉，珠稱夜光。兩岸蘆花齊點首，雲騰致雨。一條江水伴鷗飛，露結為霜。山僧於此，盡情吐露。更有一句，尚未曾道。會麼，那邊不坐空王殿，爭肯耘苗向日輪。寂後，門人於宏治十一年戊午，建塔於衛輝府輝縣白鹿山之白雲寺左。六祖下第三十一世六祖下第三十一世德安府隨州關子嶺龍泉無聞絕學明聰禪師德安府隨州關子嶺龍泉無聞絕學明聰禪師邵武奚氏子，母吳。十七出家，二十受具，習止觀、唯識論。一日，有宿衲相詰曰：大通智勝佛，十劫坐道場。佛法不現前，不得成佛道。其意如何？師依文而答，宿譏訶之。師從此疑情頓發，坐臥不安。經六載，一日聞馬嘶，大悟。遂往見天奇，奇可之。住後，上堂。僧問雲門：如何是一代時教？門曰：對一說。龍泉則不然，若有問：如何是一代時教？劈脊便打。曰：合取狗口。僧問：如何是本來面目？師曰：石香亭。曰：便恁麼去時如何？師曰：喪却了也。問：今朝四月八日，天下叢林皆慶如來聖誕。未審如來何處降生？師於几畫圓相示之。笑巖寶侍師圍爐次，師曰：人人有箇本來父母，子之父母今在何處？巖曰：一火焚之。師曰：恁麼則子無父母耶？巖曰：有則有，佛眼󳬇不見。師曰：子還見不？巖曰：不見。師曰

Senses.Explanation: Buddha Great Penetrating Wisdom Victory is the named Buddha invoked through the formula about sitting at the site of the Way for ten kalpas while the buddha teaching has not yet appeared. Baizhang Huaihai reads “kalpa” as being held up or dwelling, while Yongjue Yuanxian says the ten kalpas mark completeness and passing beyond them marks not sticking to completeness. An old monk's use of the formula drives Wuwen Mingcong's six-year inquiry.

Entries.SourceTerm: 大道只在目前，要且目前難睹

Senses.PreferredTarget: The Great Way is right before your eyes, yet what is before your eyes is hard to see
AlternateTargets: The Great Way is immediately in view, but what is in view is difficult to discern
SearchAliases: great way before eyes hard to see
right before eyes difficult to recognize
Senses.Note: The line places the Great Way before the hearer’s eyes and at once says that the obvious is difficult to recognize. In these sermons the speaker often raises a staff, points to sights or sounds, or asks the audience to say why something so near remains unseen.

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 眼覷著，覷著即錯。如是，則諸人拄杖子畢竟在什麼處？若會得，卻來方丈裡通個消息。」遂轉身歸方丈。晚參。「今宵臘月三十晚，無論貧賤與富貴，都來無事掛心頭，一味打辦度年耳。古人以喻爾我林下人一生參學，到臨命終時亦一味只要度生死且如度年。人人知道來日來年相見，秪如臨命終時，死了、燒了，又向何處相見？」良久復云：「死了、燒了，向何處相見？」乃起身出堂。入堂入堂新建彌勒內院，安禪眾入堂，舉：「仰山夢升彌勒內院，見堂中諸位皆足，唯空第二位。仰山就位而坐，眾中一尊者出云：『今當第二位說法。』仰山即出，白槌云：『摩訶衍法，離四句、絕百非。謹白。』於時眾皆散去。仰山舉似溈山，溈山云：『子已入聖位。』今日悟上座入堂，不待汝等舉白，卻自打鼓要說。」遂舉起扇云：「喚作扇子則觸，不喚作扇子則背。」良久，眾佇立，師云：「悟上座命蹇，柰我幻有老人去世，無處舉似得、無處說得。既無處舉得、無處說得，則無有人證明得。姑待眾兄弟有個會處互相證明。謹白，珍重。」入堂。「大道只在目前，要且目前難睹。且既目前難睹，在甚麼處？」以拄杖指云：「三條椽下，七尺單前，欲知大道真體，人人各自摸取。」便歸方丈。入堂，與眾向火次，云：「當初趙州和尚道：『老僧三十年前在南方行腳時，於火爐頭有個無賓主話，直至如今無人舉著。』老僧今日得得入來舉，眾中有證明底試證明看。有麼有麼？」良久，眾無出，師云：「恁麼則悟上座失利。」遂歸方丈。入堂，佛乘等請開示心、佛、眾生之旨，師云：「古人道心、佛、眾生三無差別者，大端離心外別無有佛、眾生可得，離佛外別無有心、眾生可得，離眾生外別無有心、佛可得，一體三名、三名一體。然據老僧看來，即今要且不是心、不是佛、不是眾生，復乘個甚麼？」乃翻倒几案，歸方丈。弘遠禪人送壽昌和尚語錄，師讀至自慶云：「倏爾沾嘗曹洞水，似酪涼心。」遂持入堂，謂眾云：「此老正如鼴鼠飲河，豈知大鵬劈海？老僧若見他恁麼道，劈脊一棒，使伊和心嘔出，然後更與一棒，乃云：『前一棒即不問諸人，且道後一棒是賞伊？罰伊？』若解斷得，是克家之子；設作甘與不甘，非吾種草。」入堂，舉：「《圓覺經》：『居一切時不起妄念，於諸妄心亦不息滅。住妄想境不加了知，於無了知不辨真實。』且道釋迦老子在甚麼處作活計？」一僧云：「某甲不然。」師云：「好個不然，秪是你不知落處在。

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 似富嫌千口少、貧恨一身多，爭似香林這裏園無半莖菜、廩無一粒米，信手拈將來供養諸賢者？阿呵呵！真快活，夜半鐘聲敲未斷，清晨齊唱太平歌。」復舉：「鏡清問僧：『近離甚處？』僧云：『三峰。』清云：『夏在甚處？』僧云：『五峰。』清云：『放你三十棒。』僧云：『過在什麼處？』清云：『為你出一叢林、入一叢林。』」師云：「出一叢林、入一叢林，無怪其然，只是清老棒頭至今無有落處。」示眾。舉：「僧問巖頭：『三界兢起時如何？』頭云：『坐卻著。』僧云：『未審師意如何？』頭云：『移取廬山來向你道。』」師云：「者老宿向須彌頂上撐舟、大洋海底走馬，雖則快便難逢，不免和泥合水。設有問山僧：『三界兢起時如何？』向伊道：『看腳下。』『未審師意如何？』劈脊便棒。且道與古人是同是別？」示眾。舉南嶽讓禪師參六祖因緣，師云：「輕輕一句，凝結八秋，驀地知非，翻成塗毒。不假修證，如桂月之高輝；染汙不得，似驪珠之朗耀。只如諸佛之所護念，且道護念箇甚麼？」良久，云：「露。」示眾。「大道只在目前，要且目前難睹，欲識大道真體，不離聲色言語。」驀豎拄杖云：「拄杖子聞恁麼舉，不覺手舞足蹈，走入諸人鼻孔裏，默自念云：『有佛處不得住，無佛處急走過。』你諸人還知麼？設若不知，且看興化見同參來，纔上法堂，化便喝，僧亦喝，化又喝，僧復喝，化近前拈棒，僧又喝，化云：『你看這瞎漢猶作主在。』僧擬議，化直打出法堂。又僧問：『者僧有何相觸忤？』化云：『適來見他也有權、也有實、也有照、也有用，我將手向伊面前橫兩遭，到這裏去不得。是這般瞎漢，不打更待何時？』」師云：「這老宿雖則欺胡瞞漢、逞俊一時，殊不知萬劫泥犁甘心領受。何故？可憐不遇攀花手，狼藉枝頭多少香。」晚參。舉：「仰山法堂坐次，見僧從外來，問訊了，向東邊叉手立，以目視山，山乃垂下左足；僧卻過西邊叉手立，山垂下右足；僧向中間叉手立，山收足。僧禮拜，山曰：『老僧住此，未曾打著一人。』拈棒便打，僧騰空而去。」師云：「仰山雖則善應來機，爭奈隨邪逐惡？者僧縱然乘空而去，要且當面受瞞。還委悉麼？誰家別館池塘裏，一對鴛鴦畫不成。」晚參。舉：「雲門云：『若說菩提真如解脫，是燒楓香供養你；若說佛說祖，是燒黃熟香供養你；若說超佛越祖之談，是燒餅香供養你。皈依佛、法、僧，下去。』」師云：「雲門燒香供養，要且不是好心。香林

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 今人又撐持個什麼？莫是撐持一芥園林、千年殿閣麼？不可錯認。莫是三藏十二部經、千七百則公案麼？陳年曆日且放過一邊。莫是地水火風、根塵識性麼？也是隔靴搔癢，總未端的。須知靈源湛寂，物我自如，彌淪千古，廓徹十虛，人人本具，個個不無。名得狀得，翻成畫餅；聞得見得，何異騎驢？咫尺龍華人不識，依然處處得逢渠。」拋拄杖，下座。西堂知幻、知藏心鏡、悅眾慧髻設齋，請上堂。問：「如來為一大事因緣出現於世，出世分明即不問，如何是大事因緣？」師云：「天上有星皆拱北。」進云：「秪為一花特拈出，枝頭千古惹春風。」師云：「賣弄不少。」進云：「大事已蒙師指示，光揚祖道又若何？」師豎拂子，云：「見麼？」進云：「某甲也從這裏來。」師云：「蝦跳不出斗。」問：「如何是著力句？」師云：「一羽重千觔。」進云：「如何是轉身句？」師云：「面南看北斗。」進云：「如何是親切句？」師云：「朝來喫粥夜來眠。」進云：「不是一番寒徹骨，怎得梅花撲鼻香？」師云：「三十年後來相見。」乃云：「大道只在目前，要且目前難睹；禪機獨超物外，依然聲色言語。語亦通，默亦通，高提鈯斧臥孤峰；逆亦是，順亦是，布袋橫拖入鬧市。截佛祖爪牙，展衲僧巴鼻，八十老翁入場屋，等閒不是小兒戲。」復舉：「僧問睦州云：『一氣轉得一大藏教，是否？』州云：『有甚饆饠䭔子？快把將來。』」師云：「這僧野老獻芹，睦州饑人得膳，不須百味調和，便與一口吞盡。簡點將來，也是鼯鼠飲河，只得一飽。倘問山僧：『一氣轉一大藏教，是否？』向伊道：『白牯黧奴，普同供養。』」下座。信官評謂顧公請上堂。僧問：「賢邑侯今日設齋，請師舉揚佛法，敢問如何是佛法？」師云：「快睹甘棠樹。」進云：「一方表率，萬古流芳。」師云：「欣聆單父琴。」進云：「師子窟中生師子，未曾哮吼亦驚人。」師云：「兩彩一賽。」乃云：「昔日靈山會上，如來以佛法付囑國王大臣永遠護持，庶佛日長輝，宗風丕振。今則一會儼然，畢竟宗風作麼生振？」豎拂子，云：「會麼？世尊拈花，徒標形影；達磨面壁，早涉程途。引得兒孫不唧溜，人人依樣畫葫蘆。臨濟喝、德山棒，總是一場乾打鬨；禾山鼓、雪峰毬，惱亂春風尚未休。」復擊，云：「惟此一著，天無私蓋、地無私載，在凡不減一毫、在聖不增一毫，有時現尊榮身、有時現威武身，來作仙溪雨露，擢為帝室股肱，應彼應此，如日循環則固是

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 超佛越祖，奚必雪山六載然後始悟？是汝諸公知他悟箇甚麼？金生麗水，玉出崑岡。」元旦，上堂。問：「春王歲首物咸亨，斬新條令事如何？」師云：「棒頭有眼明如日。」進云：「天道和平添吉慶，歌謠萬里樂無為。」師云：「句下無私幾箇知？」問：「王登寶殿，野老歡呼，祝聖一句如何舉揚？」師云：「行坐春風堆裏，盤桓流水橋邊。」進云：「惠風和藹，舜日增輝，新年佛法，請師垂示。」師云：「楊柳欣逢知己，梅花猶是故人。」進云：「曉開柳眼窺晴旭，臘綻梅花占早春。」師云：「更道不堪。」乃云：「今有三般好事：一遇春王歲首，萬物咸亨；二為天道和平，八方安泰；三是常舒齋嚫，大眾歡呼。山僧自來棒頭有眼，不妨行坐春風堆裏；句下無私，何礙盤桓流水橋邊？一問一荅，亦足以暢敘幽情；一歌一謠，更不知有人間世。你道憑何節目便爾如然？」揮拂，云：「日出海門東畔，山河燦爛一新；煙銷谷口鳥啼，春漏泄風光。卻甚楊柳欣逢知己，梅花猶是故人？新年佛法太分明，端的何須再問？」解制，值雪，上堂。「大道只在目前，要且目前難睹。雪覆萬年松徑，明暗奚分？雲遮一帶峰巒，正偏孰辯？一色邊坐住，固非本地風光；淨白地安身，豈是到家消息？何況擔囊頂笠、航海梯山，又成得箇甚麼邊事？大眾！要識大道麼？」喝一喝，云：「切忌癡狂外邊走。」李護法華誕，祈嗣，請上堂。「山色蒙茸，春光明媚，惟有箇事，迥超物外。莊嚴壽量，本乎天然，福慧苗裔，隨身自在。無量壽佛，那共論乎劫塵？多子如來，不與方乎境界。等閒垂一機一境，立一事一法，皆可以添算今時，流芳後代。阿呵呵！會不會？好看清白傳家計。」結夏，曇瑞禪德請上堂。「一句了然，迥超百億；一言解脫，頓悟真常。善財登樓閣而明心，留得虛窗前夜月，三更依舊照茆堂；龍女獻寶珠以成佛，等閒識得東風面，萬紫千紅總是春。所以道：迷時迷卻悟底，悟時悟卻迷底。青龍者裏直饒迷悟雙忘、聖凡俱泯，猶是草菴止宿、門外周遊。未審如何是到家消息？踏得故鄉田地穩，不妨隨處現優曇。」雷護法得子，請上堂。豎拂云：「只此育聖生賢，超宗越祖，輪王得以御天下，四臣得以牧萬民，父得以慈，子得以孝。以此修身，身無不正；以此齊家，家無不和；以此祈福，福無不臻。求智慧得智慧，求男女得男女，求長壽得長壽。你道拂子有甚奇特，如此神通廣大？」擊香几云：「水向石邊流出冷，風從花裏過來香。」韋

Senses.Explanation: The Great Way is right before your eyes, yet what is before your eyes is hard to see turns nearness into a test of recognition. Miyun says the pair, points with his staff, and directs his listeners to the seats in front of them. Chuiwan continues the line with birdsong and a heron on sand, then asks what sound and language mean. Fogu recites the larger saying and raises his staff before the assembly. Lianfeng gives the line before speaking of seeing and hearing in a sermon. Meixi names moonlight, wind in bamboo, and the present exchange, then asks where the Great Way is. Eryin raises a staff and sounds it while asking the same question. Hansong places the pair in a snowy scene and warns against seeking elsewhere.

Senses.PreferredTarget: The great Way is right before your eyes, yet what is before your eyes is hard to see
AlternateTargets: The great Way is here in plain sight, but still difficult to perceive
SearchAliases: great Way right before eyes hard to see
Way in plain sight difficult to perceive
Senses.Note: The saying puts the great Way directly before the eyes, then says that what is directly before them is hard to see. Later masters repeat it while using what is already at hand: Baiyun holds up a staff, Wumen uses a whisk to show sound and form, and Chushi points to ordinary temple things. Their demonstrations make the difficulty a question of how one attends, rather than how far away the Way is.

Occurrences.Kwic: 作麼生道？乃云：野老不知堯舜力，𭽸𭽸打皷祭江神。上堂，舉：僧問六祖：黃梅意旨是什麼人得？六祖云：會佛法人得。僧云：師還得否？祖云：我不得。僧云：為什麼不得？祖云：我不會佛法。大眾！還識祖師麼？上堂，舉：長沙和尚遊山迴，首座問：和尚甚處去來？長沙云：始隨芳艸去，又逐落花迴。首座云：大似春意。長沙云：也勝秋露滴芙蕖。大眾，且道長沙在春夏秋冬中，不在春夏秋冬中？要會麼？一氣不言含有象，萬靈何處謝無私。上堂，舉僧問洞山和尚：寒暑到來如何迴避？洞山云：何不向無寒暑處去？僧云：如何是無寒暑處？洞山云：寒時寒殺闍黎，熱時熱殺闍黎。洞山老人偏向枯木上生春，作麼生下手？白雲：今日與你下手。今日是開鑪。上堂，舉：百丈和尚云：汝等為我開田，吾為汝等說大義。一日，眾開田了，云：開田已竟，請和尚說大義。百丈展開兩手，行數步。大眾！百丈如是說大義，諸人還記得麼？今日白雲重為諸人說過：常憐百丈解開田，今古行人手裡傳。誰道舌頭曾不動，五音六律太周旋。上堂，云：大道只在目前，要且目前難覩，欲識大道真體，不離聲色言語。拈起拄杖，云：者箇是拄杖子，阿那箇是大道真體？將箇什麼識？想你者一隊漆桶，臈月三十日只認得驢鞍橋作阿爺下頷。乃喝云：去。上堂云：言之者失其真，知之者返其愚，有之者乖其性，無之者傷其軀。若也會得，因風吹火，用力不多；若也不會，秋水共長天一色。然雖如是，有時乘好月，不覺過滄州。演首座受四面請，上堂云：年年秋暑甚如初，何事清凉特有餘？盡是當人心地感，不虗把手在龍舒。且道把手一句作麼生道？良久云：行到水窮處，坐看雲起時。上堂。云：秋色凄清，早晚愈凉，信知節氣不相饒。林間學道之士，飢則喫飯，寒則添衣，殊不知世間有苦樂者。且道如何得知苦樂去？乃云：只知事逐眼前過，不覺老從頭上來。興道者開田迴，上堂云：三歲區區弄水泥，捎裩擗袴又扶犁，滿倉収稻方歸院，一任禪和韗肚皮。且道韗底是禪？是飯？乃云：因風吹火，用力不多。上堂。云：少一滴不得，剩一滴不得，且道是什麼人分上事？良久，云：日日日東上，夜夜月西流。上堂，云：文字一般樣，語話一般樣，聲勢一般，理趣一般，為什麼却道他未在？乃云：只為鼻孔大，頭向下。白雲端和尚語錄卷二白雲端和尚語錄卷三偈頌偈頌世尊世尊指天指地行七步，雙放雙収重夾注。槨中錦上更添花，直至如今垂雨露。達

Occurrences.Kwic: 、心病、佛病、祖病，一時頓愈。雖然如是，知恩者少，負恩者多。謝般若和尚上堂，舉僧問智門：如何是般若體？門云：蚌含明月。又問：如何是般若用？門云：兔子懷胎。師云：大眾！智門美則美矣，善則未善。今日忽有人問焦山：如何是般若體？只向他道：烈焰亘天。又問：如何是般若用？向他道：一味蠱毒。近之者燎却面門，甞之者喪却性命。大眾各自照顧。上堂，舉趙州和尚示眾云：南來者與他下載，北來者與他上載，大似世情看冷暖，人義逐高低。又慈受和尚云：南來者與他一面咲，北來者與他一面咲，大似歡喜廝算，咲裏有刀。若是焦山又且不然，南來者以平常待之，北來者以平常待之，也不嗔、也不咲，也無下、也無高。何故？清平世界不用干戈。上堂。人情濃厚道情微，道用人情世豈知？空有人情無道用，人情能得幾多時？龍牙和尚恁麼告報，太煞老婆心切。雖然如是，人情即不問，如何是道用？山僧口門窄，煩木上座為諸人說破。卓拄杖一下。平江府開元禪寺語錄平江府開元禪寺語錄侍者普覺錄陞座，祝聖罷，乃云：大道只在目前，要且目前難覩，欲識大道真體，不離聲色言語。拂子，擊禪牀，云：這箇是聲。豎拂子，云：這箇是色。喚什麼作大道？長將日月為天眼，指出須彌作壽山。復舉：三聖道：逢人則出，出則不為人。興化道：逢人則不出，出則便為人。師云：且道開元為人即是？不為人即是？大事管你不得，小事各自擔當。上堂。動絃別曲，葉落知秋。禾山打鼓，雪峰輥毬。睦州擔板，投子提油。趙州狗子，溈山牯牛。青原垂足，俱胝指頭。一隊破落戶，各自逞風流。若到開元門下，打教棒折未休。何故？豈不見道：重賞之下，必有勇夫。解夏，上堂。布袋頭開今日始，滿目江山秋色裏，驀然踏斷艸鞋跟，元來却是自家底。上堂：信脚行去絕埃塵，信手拈來用得親，信口道出驚天地，信心悟入獨超羣。直饒恁麼，正好來山僧處喫痛棒。何故？要識真金火裏看。冬至，上堂：陰極陽生，日添一線。拈拄杖：獨有山僧拄杖子，不屬陰陽遷變。卓杖一下。上堂，舉：僧問香林：如何是衲衣下事？林云：臘月火燒山。今日忽有人問開元：如何是衲衣下事？只向他道：但得雪消去，自然春到來。元正，上堂：昨日去年去，今朝今歲來。去年去不去，今歲來不來。且道不涉去來一句又作麼生？樓上已吹新歲角，堂前猶點舊年燈。觀音生日，上堂。現種種形，說種種法。形法皆非，假名菩薩。更於諸相覔圓通

Occurrences.Kwic: ？還會麼？泣露千般艸，唫風一樣松。上堂。行不犯之令，明古今風月。靈機常獨耀，萬象悉澄徹。更說什麼正法眼藏，瞎驢邊滅。無計較中翻成計較，無途轍中翻成途轍。一時與你截斷秤鎚硬似鐵。別別，八月秋，何處熱。謝知事，上堂。萬里浮雲捲碧天，年年此夜十分圓，令人轉憶寒山子，說似吾心恰宛然。所以道：欲明恁麼事，還他恁麼人；若是恁麼人，須明恁麼事。便能以此心相照、以此心相知，扶持野老無盡家風，成就叢林萬世基業。其把定也，離念絕塵，更無滲漏；其放行也，光生瓦礫，和氣靄然，高低普應，前後無差。且道此人成得箇什麼邊事？還委悉麼？將此身心奉塵剎，是則名為報佛恩。上堂：十五日已前且恁麼折合，更不周繇者也。十五日已後見成公案，未曾動著，正當十五日。諸人作麼生通箇消息？直饒向朕兆未萌、文彩未彰時會去，正落第二月。且作麼生是第一月？還會麼？九年孤坐少人識，千古風光照天地。上堂，僧問：如何是大道真源？師云：和泥合水。僧云：便恁麼去時如何？師云：截斷草鞋跟。師乃云：大道只在目前，要且目前難覩。欲識大道真體，不離聲色言語。風吹不入處，和泥合水；和泥合水處，風吹不入。如今不免又向頭上安頭。乃豎起拂子云：還見麼？者箇是色。復呵呵大笑云：者箇是聲。大道真體在什麼處？繡出鴛鴦無背面，不知誰解覓金針？上堂：眼裏不著沙，耳裏不著水，堪笑老俱胝，無端豎一指。諸禪德，且道是誰解笑者？還會麼？閙市拶出憍尸迦，吃嘹舌頭三千里。上堂：大智圓明，體無向背。凝然湛寂，彌滿太虗。覆葢乾坤，常光獨露。削蹤滅跡，離相絕名。正當恁麼時，本地不動一句作麼生道？一切水月一月攝。上堂，僧問：請師答話。師云：火雲燒空。僧云：且道虗空還有變易也無？師云：飽粥，飽飯。僧云：恁麼則有變易去也。師云：客作漢有什麼變易？師乃云：炎暑蒸人汗似湯，鹽官用底豈尋常？輕搖休問犀牛在，拈出清風宇宙涼。諸禪德！向什麼處見鹽官老子？若也見得，恩大難酬；其或未然，汗流浹背會施力，一到中秋便負心。上堂，舉：馬大師翫月次，問西堂：正當恁麼時如何？堂云：正好修行。次問百丈，丈云：正好供養。又問南泉，泉抽身歸眾。馬祖云：經歸藏，禪歸海，惟有普願獨超物外。師云：奇怪！諸禪德！馬駒踏殺天下人，一摑直須一掌血。及乎三大士各展家風，不覺翻成老婆心切，叢林浩浩商量，盡道翫月話奇特，簡點將來，克繇尀

Occurrences.Kwic: 恩方解報恩。進云：昨夜清風生八極，今朝流水漲前溪。師云：追風天馬戴麒麟。進云：非但左司承此善，學人禮拜謝師恩。師云：未放你在。僧禮拜，師云：脚跟下失却。師乃云：寶劒揮空，乾坤失色，掀翻是非窠窟，截斷生死根株。有佛處不得住，地久天長；無佛處急走過，河清海晏。三千里外一句全提，更無絲毫滲漏，堪與佛祖為師作箇人天牓樣。正恁麼時，轉凡成聖一句作麼生道？委悉麼？萬古碧潭空界月，再三撈摝始應知。入院，上堂。僧問：遠離光孝，來赴妙嚴。如何是不動尊？師云：一別蓮城五日程。進云：竹密不妨流水過，山高豈礙白雲飛？師云：老僧不曾動步。進云：今日得聞於未聞？師云：急須吐却。進云：昔日楊岐，今朝和尚。師云：這裏著不得。進云：爭柰公案現成？師云：將謂你是箇漢。僧云：劄。師云：未在。師乃云：孤峰萬仞，鳥道虗玄，名利杳忘，是非頓絕。直得猿吟古木，虎嘯幽巖，碧落青霄，道人活計。雖然恁麼，更須知有人境俱奪向上一竅。乃竪拂，云：天上有星皆拱北，人間無水不朝東。上堂。大道只在目前，要且目前難覩。欲識大道真體，不離聲色言語，言語動用了無交涉。且大道真體在什麼處？良久，云：可憐傅大士，處處失樓閣。出隊歸，上堂。透過鐵壁銀山、紅塵閙市，全彰古佛家風；經過酒肆茶坊，突出衲僧巴鼻。冷笑諸方寒灰枯木，坐在無魂必死之地。妙嚴有些子神通，為汝諸人出氣。卓拄杖，云：三十年弄馬騎，却被瞎驢受記。又卓一卓，下座。上堂。九年面壁，壞却東土兒孫；隻履西歸，鈍置黃面老子。以拄杖劃一劃，云：石牛欄古路，一馬生三寅。上堂。黃蘗老婆，大愚饒舌。佛法無多子，正眼瞎驢滅。驀拈拄杖，云：妙嚴突出拄杖，三人證龜成鼈。以拄杖卓一卓，云：拄杖子，善甄別，硬却脊梁，莫教漏泄。觀音菩薩將錢買胡餅，放下却是一塊生鐵。遂擲下拄杖，下座。上堂。大丈夫須猛烈，打破從前伎倆，直下斬釘截鐵，拈却佛祖機，󳫠却繫驢橛。豈不見睦州為人太親切，拶得雲門脚折，後來兒孫不辨端倪，却向推門處辨別。若也恁麼參禪，驢年未得休歇，妙嚴不惜眉毛，與你當頭拈出。驀拈拄杖擲下，云：南贍部洲人常在，北󳬂單越上堂，舉：僧問大隋：如何是和尚家風？隋云：赤土畫簸箕。僧云：如何是赤土畫簸箕？隋云：簸箕有唇，米跳不出。師云：諸人還知大隋落處麼？妙嚴更為頌出：簸箕有唇，米跳不出，天下衲僧赤𩨘𩪸；更須撥轉上頭關，十

Occurrences.Kwic: 竅。還委悉麼？麥秋晨氣潤，槐夏午陰清。復舉：龐居士參馬大師：不與萬法為侶是什麼人？大師云：待汝一口吸盡西江水，却向汝道。師頌云：葢天葢地一句子，馬師盡力提不起，好笑青原接石頭，逢人但問廬陵米。上堂。古人云：擬為你吞却，只為當門齒礙。如今不礙，也吞得麼？擬為你吐却，只怕咽喉小。如今不小，也吐得麼？吞得一任吞，吐得一任吐。設你吞得吐得，我更問你：是什麼乾屎橛？上堂：是凡是聖，半合半開；非佛非心，全生全殺。直似排空徤翮，萬里橫翔；透網金鱗，一絲不挂。豈不俊快衲僧？有時句到意不到，有時意到句不到，有時意句俱到，有時意句俱不到。若意句俱到，你作麼生商量？若意句俱不到，你又向什麼處𪅎󲣅？上上人來時如何點？中夏，上堂。舉龐居士云：護生須是殺，生薑不改辣，殺盡始安居，到處得逢渠。欲識箇中意，爛泥裏有刺，鐵船水上浮，鬍子沒髭須。有底見他道殺也，便道：殺佛殺祖，揀箇什麼？恁麼見解，鄭州出曹門，不如休去歇去好。忽然築著鼻孔，鐵船水上浮是真實語。上堂：大道只在目前，要且目前難覩。欲識大道真體，不離聲色言語。諸仁者！佛殿裏香爐、東司頭籌子為你說了也。憍陳如尊者醉後添杯來，我這裏聽的總是註脚。當初只謂茅長短，燒却元來地不平。上堂。彈指一下，云：這裏聞去，一根既返源，六處咸休復。眼處作耳處佛事、耳處作鼻處佛事、鼻處作舌處佛事、舌處作身處佛事、身處作意處佛事、意處作一切處佛事，畢竟是一耶？是六耶？纔有一，便有六；纔有六，便有一。此是一六之義，不可道是無也。無眼、耳、鼻、舌、身、意，無色、聲、香、味、觸、法，又不可認有也。這箇是教意？那箇是祖意？喝一喝。解夏，小參。僧問：九夏償勞，如何言薦？師云：重疊關山路。進云：便與麼去時如何？師云：江南僅有，江北絕無。乃云：數日已來可謂極熱，晚間得雨便覺清凉，熱既不從外來，凉亦非從內出，不離當處，廓爾現前，則古釋迦不先、今彌勒不後，何待精修六度始至法雲？遠涉僧祇，方階佛果，便可於一毫端現寶王剎、坐微塵裏轉大法輪，有時拈一莖草作丈六金身用、有時拈丈六金身作一莖草用，如斯坐夏，功不浪施，端的蠟人冰，純成鐵彈子。功圓果滿一句作麼生道？一片月生海，幾家人上樓？復舉：僧辭歸宗，宗云：什麼處去？僧云：諸方學五味禪去。宗云：我這裏有一味禪。僧云：如何是一味禪？宗便打，僧云：我會也，我

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 作麼生道？乃云：野老不知堯舜力，𭽸𭽸打皷祭江神。上堂，舉：僧問六祖：黃梅意旨是什麼人得？六祖云：會佛法人得。僧云：師還得否？祖云：我不得。僧云：為什麼不得？祖云：我不會佛法。大眾！還識祖師麼？上堂，舉：長沙和尚遊山迴，首座問：和尚甚處去來？長沙云：始隨芳艸去，又逐落花迴。首座云：大似春意。長沙云：也勝秋露滴芙蕖。大眾，且道長沙在春夏秋冬中，不在春夏秋冬中？要會麼？一氣不言含有象，萬靈何處謝無私。上堂，舉僧問洞山和尚：寒暑到來如何迴避？洞山云：何不向無寒暑處去？僧云：如何是無寒暑處？洞山云：寒時寒殺闍黎，熱時熱殺闍黎。洞山老人偏向枯木上生春，作麼生下手？白雲：今日與你下手。今日是開鑪。上堂，舉：百丈和尚云：汝等為我開田，吾為汝等說大義。一日，眾開田了，云：開田已竟，請和尚說大義。百丈展開兩手，行數步。大眾！百丈如是說大義，諸人還記得麼？今日白雲重為諸人說過：常憐百丈解開田，今古行人手裡傳。誰道舌頭曾不動，五音六律太周旋。上堂，云：大道只在目前，要且目前難覩，欲識大道真體，不離聲色言語。拈起拄杖，云：者箇是拄杖子，阿那箇是大道真體？將箇什麼識？想你者一隊漆桶，臈月三十日只認得驢鞍橋作阿爺下頷。乃喝云：去。上堂云：言之者失其真，知之者返其愚，有之者乖其性，無之者傷其軀。若也會得，因風吹火，用力不多；若也不會，秋水共長天一色。然雖如是，有時乘好月，不覺過滄州。演首座受四面請，上堂云：年年秋暑甚如初，何事清凉特有餘？盡是當人心地感，不虗把手在龍舒。且道把手一句作麼生道？良久云：行到水窮處，坐看雲起時。上堂。云：秋色凄清，早晚愈凉，信知節氣不相饒。林間學道之士，飢則喫飯，寒則添衣，殊不知世間有苦樂者。且道如何得知苦樂去？乃云：只知事逐眼前過，不覺老從頭上來。興道者開田迴，上堂云：三歲區區弄水泥，捎裩擗袴又扶犁，滿倉収稻方歸院，一任禪和韗肚皮。且道韗底是禪？是飯？乃云：因風吹火，用力不多。上堂。云：少一滴不得，剩一滴不得，且道是什麼人分上事？良久，云：日日日東上，夜夜月西流。上堂，云：文字一般樣，語話一般樣，聲勢一般，理趣一般，為什麼却道他未在？乃云：只為鼻孔大，頭向下。白雲端和尚語錄卷二白雲端和尚語錄卷三偈頌偈頌世尊世尊指天指地行七步，雙放雙収重夾注。槨中錦上更添花，直至如今垂雨露。達

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 、心病、佛病、祖病，一時頓愈。雖然如是，知恩者少，負恩者多。謝般若和尚上堂，舉僧問智門：如何是般若體？門云：蚌含明月。又問：如何是般若用？門云：兔子懷胎。師云：大眾！智門美則美矣，善則未善。今日忽有人問焦山：如何是般若體？只向他道：烈焰亘天。又問：如何是般若用？向他道：一味蠱毒。近之者燎却面門，甞之者喪却性命。大眾各自照顧。上堂，舉趙州和尚示眾云：南來者與他下載，北來者與他上載，大似世情看冷暖，人義逐高低。又慈受和尚云：南來者與他一面咲，北來者與他一面咲，大似歡喜廝算，咲裏有刀。若是焦山又且不然，南來者以平常待之，北來者以平常待之，也不嗔、也不咲，也無下、也無高。何故？清平世界不用干戈。上堂。人情濃厚道情微，道用人情世豈知？空有人情無道用，人情能得幾多時？龍牙和尚恁麼告報，太煞老婆心切。雖然如是，人情即不問，如何是道用？山僧口門窄，煩木上座為諸人說破。卓拄杖一下。平江府開元禪寺語錄平江府開元禪寺語錄侍者普覺錄陞座，祝聖罷，乃云：大道只在目前，要且目前難覩，欲識大道真體，不離聲色言語。拂子，擊禪牀，云：這箇是聲。豎拂子，云：這箇是色。喚什麼作大道？長將日月為天眼，指出須彌作壽山。復舉：三聖道：逢人則出，出則不為人。興化道：逢人則不出，出則便為人。師云：且道開元為人即是？不為人即是？大事管你不得，小事各自擔當。上堂。動絃別曲，葉落知秋。禾山打鼓，雪峰輥毬。睦州擔板，投子提油。趙州狗子，溈山牯牛。青原垂足，俱胝指頭。一隊破落戶，各自逞風流。若到開元門下，打教棒折未休。何故？豈不見道：重賞之下，必有勇夫。解夏，上堂。布袋頭開今日始，滿目江山秋色裏，驀然踏斷艸鞋跟，元來却是自家底。上堂：信脚行去絕埃塵，信手拈來用得親，信口道出驚天地，信心悟入獨超羣。直饒恁麼，正好來山僧處喫痛棒。何故？要識真金火裏看。冬至，上堂：陰極陽生，日添一線。拈拄杖：獨有山僧拄杖子，不屬陰陽遷變。卓杖一下。上堂，舉：僧問香林：如何是衲衣下事？林云：臘月火燒山。今日忽有人問開元：如何是衲衣下事？只向他道：但得雪消去，自然春到來。元正，上堂：昨日去年去，今朝今歲來。去年去不去，今歲來不來。且道不涉去來一句又作麼生？樓上已吹新歲角，堂前猶點舊年燈。觀音生日，上堂。現種種形，說種種法。形法皆非，假名菩薩。更於諸相覔圓通

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: ？還會麼？泣露千般艸，唫風一樣松。上堂。行不犯之令，明古今風月。靈機常獨耀，萬象悉澄徹。更說什麼正法眼藏，瞎驢邊滅。無計較中翻成計較，無途轍中翻成途轍。一時與你截斷秤鎚硬似鐵。別別，八月秋，何處熱。謝知事，上堂。萬里浮雲捲碧天，年年此夜十分圓，令人轉憶寒山子，說似吾心恰宛然。所以道：欲明恁麼事，還他恁麼人；若是恁麼人，須明恁麼事。便能以此心相照、以此心相知，扶持野老無盡家風，成就叢林萬世基業。其把定也，離念絕塵，更無滲漏；其放行也，光生瓦礫，和氣靄然，高低普應，前後無差。且道此人成得箇什麼邊事？還委悉麼？將此身心奉塵剎，是則名為報佛恩。上堂：十五日已前且恁麼折合，更不周繇者也。十五日已後見成公案，未曾動著，正當十五日。諸人作麼生通箇消息？直饒向朕兆未萌、文彩未彰時會去，正落第二月。且作麼生是第一月？還會麼？九年孤坐少人識，千古風光照天地。上堂，僧問：如何是大道真源？師云：和泥合水。僧云：便恁麼去時如何？師云：截斷草鞋跟。師乃云：大道只在目前，要且目前難覩。欲識大道真體，不離聲色言語。風吹不入處，和泥合水；和泥合水處，風吹不入。如今不免又向頭上安頭。乃豎起拂子云：還見麼？者箇是色。復呵呵大笑云：者箇是聲。大道真體在什麼處？繡出鴛鴦無背面，不知誰解覓金針？上堂：眼裏不著沙，耳裏不著水，堪笑老俱胝，無端豎一指。諸禪德，且道是誰解笑者？還會麼？閙市拶出憍尸迦，吃嘹舌頭三千里。上堂：大智圓明，體無向背。凝然湛寂，彌滿太虗。覆葢乾坤，常光獨露。削蹤滅跡，離相絕名。正當恁麼時，本地不動一句作麼生道？一切水月一月攝。上堂，僧問：請師答話。師云：火雲燒空。僧云：且道虗空還有變易也無？師云：飽粥，飽飯。僧云：恁麼則有變易去也。師云：客作漢有什麼變易？師乃云：炎暑蒸人汗似湯，鹽官用底豈尋常？輕搖休問犀牛在，拈出清風宇宙涼。諸禪德！向什麼處見鹽官老子？若也見得，恩大難酬；其或未然，汗流浹背會施力，一到中秋便負心。上堂，舉：馬大師翫月次，問西堂：正當恁麼時如何？堂云：正好修行。次問百丈，丈云：正好供養。又問南泉，泉抽身歸眾。馬祖云：經歸藏，禪歸海，惟有普願獨超物外。師云：奇怪！諸禪德！馬駒踏殺天下人，一摑直須一掌血。及乎三大士各展家風，不覺翻成老婆心切，叢林浩浩商量，盡道翫月話奇特，簡點將來，克繇尀

Senses.Explanation: The great roc spreads its wings and covers the ten isles. Dahui Zonggao gives the line as an answer; Xutang Zhiyu, Songyuan Chongyue, Baichi Xingyuan, Guxue Zhenzhe, and Chushi Fanqi use it in further answers or hall addresses. The recurring second half sets the great roc against sparrows, swallows, or a fence-side creature chirping at the edge. The corpus predominantly writes the final noun as 'isles'; Songyuan also preserves a one-work homophonous spelling, while Chushi preserves an older graph for 'cover.' Yuanwu Keqin supplies the corpus's direct lexical evidence in the Blue Cliff Record: 'At sea there are three mountains and ten isles.'

Senses.Explanation: One's life is the living stake that can be established, placed in another person's hands, or spoken of as the vital life of former buddhas. Juelang Daosheng calls planting flowers on stone easy but establishing one's life difficult. Jianfu Huai asks whether Gautama's life is in another person's hands. Liao'an Qingyu pairs the former buddhas' vital life with the later buddhas' governing rule and locates both at the tip of his raised whisk.

Senses.Explanation: Ocean of nature figures nature as an all-encompassing sea. Yongming Yanshou writes that wisdom reaches this ocean while learning penetrates the true source; the Yongzheng imperial preface uses the image to reject a merely empty stance; and Foyan Qingyuan says that the source of the Way is not far and the ocean of nature is not distant. The expression’s scope remains figurative, not a literal body of water.

Senses.PreferredTarget: Fire in its nature is true emptiness; the emptiness of nature is true fire
SearchAliases: fire in its nature is true emptiness; the emptiness of nature is true fire
Senses.Note: “Nature-fire is true emptiness; nature-emptiness is true fire” becomes pointed speech at a cremation. Poshan raises the torch for Minyan, while Faxi uses the pair to ask where the departed fire attendant Huiguang could hide. Pinjixiang voices it for a deceased elder and makes the fire disclose rather than erase. Yushan repeats the pair for a departing practitioner. In each rite the reversal connects the visible fire with the question of what can be lost.

Occurrences.Kwic: 為超法師舉火為超法師舉火性空真火，性火真空。來從此來，去復其中。法師圓寂，我等難逢。若問歸何處，白雲無定踪。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X73/X73n1449.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Wushan Jingduan. Wushan Jingduan opens the lighting of Master Chao's funeral fire with the reciprocal formula: empty by nature, true fire; fire by nature, true emptiness. He then says coming is from here and going returns within it, laments that the deceased can no longer easily be met, and answers the question of where he goes with white clouds that have no fixed track. The actual lighting and the question of departure give the formula its work. Fire and emptiness are spoken together at the fire; the passage does not claim that no flame burns or name a definite place to which the deceased has traveled. The headword is rendered: Empty by nature, true fire; fire by nature, true emptiness.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J26/J26nB184.xml). Seven-Session Recorded Sayings of Monk Muyun. Muyun Tongmen uses the same formula while lighting the cremation fire for the practitioner Jizong. He says it is pointed out directly and wholly shared, and that the wise of the ten directions enter this purport. He then addresses Jizong by name twice, telling him to throw both feet into the air and not concern himself with north, south, east or west. The pair leads into this direct funeral address, which declines to organize the departure by compass directions. Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X71/X71n1422.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Nanshi Wenxiu. Nanshi Wenxiu uses it at a senior monk's funeral fire. He opens with chanting praises in the bell tower and planting vegetables at the foot of the bed, then says that to understand directly is to be unobstructed in birth and death. The fire-and-emptiness pair follows that claim, and his final image has a tiny midge swallowing Mount Sumeru. The formula thus belongs to an address that places ordinary acts and impossibly altered scale together at cremation. The image is not a report of an insect physically consuming a mountain; likewise, the reciprocal words do not erase the burning before the listeners. The headword is rendered: Empty by nature, true fire; fire by nature, true emptiness.

Senses.Explanation: “Topple Huang Fanchuo to death” is the comic closing line of the Pan Lang backwards-donkey verse, not a report of an actual killing. Occurrences.Kwic: 平。無端業風一鼓，定業難逃，巾子峯前，無回避處，不免劄箇硬寨，直得鴉飛不度，要使不入眾數底衲僧助桀為虐，逐惡隨邪，潑除正因，凌蔑宗社。然則先帝在天之靈又且如何崇奉？將此深心奉塵剎，是則名為報佛恩。舉太宗皇帝問僧：近離甚處？僧云：臥雲菴。帝云：臥雲深處不朝天，因甚到此？僧無對。雪竇和尚代云：難迯至化。師頌云：試問臥雲深處客，不知何以答升平。蕩然至化難迯避，萬里堯天一點雲。當晚小參(問答不錄)當晚小參靈龜曳尾，拂跡跡生；霧豹澤毛，藏文文露。避喧求靜，未有其方；喧靜一如，重重關鎻。所以，古人道：今朝得到無心地，猶被無心趂出山。放一頭低，入󱈎垂手；東倒西攂，轉位回機。然雖如是，畢竟無神通菩薩足跡，如何尋覔？自是時人自遮護，先生毫髮不相瞞。上堂舉：雲居弘覺禪師將欲謝事，寺主問云：和尚去後，何人繼席？覺云：堂中簡。簡密受印記，携道具徑歸方丈。寺主以簡為揀，欲請第二座，簡遂下山。山神號泣云：還我和尚來。於是寺主追至麥莊，具禮請歸。山神復云：我和尚歸也
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X69/X69n1365.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Beijian Jujian. Beijian uses the mist-hidden leopard in his own minor sermon to expose the risk of hiding in quietude.

Senses.Explanation: The mist-hidden leopard enriches its coat while its markings remain concealed. Jue’an applies the line to an attendant who remains steady and does not feed; Binya answers a question about Linji’s shout by adding that the leopard is for now concealing its markings. Cuiyan’s appraisal of the Huangbo exchange pairs the unfed mist-hidden leopard with the courtyard bird that stores its courage until it startles people. Yingshan uses the hidden leopard as an analogy for discipline that prepares effective activity in his own instruction. Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X68/X68n1318.xml). Continued Essentials from the Sayings of Ancient Worthies. After quoting Ganzi’s exchange, Baiyun Shouduan says that Baiyun would not respond that way and repeats the comparison ‘like feeding donkeys and horses.’ Baiyun Shouduan is the utterer of this retained occurrence.

Senses.Explanation: The phrase compares receiving and feeding visitors to feeding donkeys and horses. The lay attendant Ganzi answers a comment about the difficulty of hospitality with it; Gaofeng opens the retreat boundary and says to feed the animals; Mingjue gives it as his answer before the black bean sprouts; Baiyun raises Ganzi’s case and then changes the inherited appraisal.
